passages.title: Analyst read — baby child (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's baby & child segment now has data for the first time, though the two size estimates disagree sharply: BlueWeave US$1.61bn (2024, RETAIL, LOW) vs Expert Market Research US$746.89mn (2025, RETAIL, LOW) - a 2.2x gap on what both describe as an identical scope (baby cosmetics & toiletries plus baby food and baby safety/convenience). Both therefore materially overstate the BPC-relevant segment, with no BPC-only split disclosed by either. A narrower, MFDS-sourced signal exists only for growth (see trend), not size. The two size sources also disagree on pace: BlueWeave forecasts 3.55% CAGR (2025-2031, LOW) vs Expert Market Research 6.2% (2026-2035, LOW), a 1.7x spread on the same wider-than-BPC basket. The closest read to true BPC scope is an MFDS PRODUCTION-basis figure for the 'baby/infant products' cosmetics type: +6.21% YoY in 2024 (ESTIMATE confidence, derived from two adjacent years in the same official table) - factory-gate output, not retail sell-through. A true category-wide RETAIL growth_yoy remains an open research gap. Both RETAIL size estimates bundle in baby food and safety/convenience products with no BPC-only split, so treat scale as a wide upper bound rather than a segment figure; the two forecasts and two levels do not reconcile and should not be averaged. The MFDS growth figure is PRODUCTION basis (factory-gate, ESTIMATE confidence), not a retail category growth rate.

passages.title: Analyst read — baby child (India)
passages.text: India's baby & child segment now has data for the first time, with two size estimates in outright contradiction: IMARC US$4.82bn (2025, RETAIL, LOW) on a WIDER basket that includes baby food, versus Maximize Market Research US$14.17bn (2024, RETAIL, LOW) on a basket that explicitly EXCLUDES baby food - the narrower-scope source gives the much larger number, which the two sources do not reconcile. A single-company proxy exists alongside: Chicco India (Artsana), a premium/imported player, reported over 35% revenue growth in FY25 (MEDIUM confidence, CEO-quoted) - a floor figure for one brand, not the market. Forecast CAGRs also disagree: IMARC 9.17% (2026-2034, LOW) vs Maximize Market Research 14.35% (2024-2030, LOW), a 1.6x spread on the same contradictory bases. No category-wide RETAIL growth_yoy figure exists; Chicco India's >35% is one premium-imported company, not the market. The two size estimates do not merely vary, they contradict outright (the wider-scope source is smaller), so India baby_child scale is unresolved in the data, not just imprecise; organised-vs-unorganised coverage is unstated by either. Category-wide growth_yoy remains an open research gap.

passages.title: Analyst read — baby child (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both sides now carry a RETAIL market-size figure, but each side's own two sources already contradict each other (KR 2.2x apart, IN 2.9x apart with the wider-scope source reading smaller) - comparing KR to IN on top of two unresolved internal conflicts would compound the uncertainty, so no KR-vs-IN size comparison is attempted here. No [CORRIDOR]-tagged data point exists for baby_child in either file.

passages.title: Analyst read — bath shower (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's bath & shower segment now has a domestic retail size for the first time: US$357.35mn (2025, RETAIL, LOW confidence, Expert Market Research), on a scope EMR describes as shower gel/bubble wash, bath salts, bar soap and bath bombs - narrower than a full bath & shower category, and EMR does not state channel coverage or duty-free treatment. A separate HIGH-confidence MFDS PRODUCTION figure exists for the wider '인체 세정용' (personal/body cleansing) product type, KRW 2.077tn in 2024 (~US$1.405bn), but that type bundles facial foam cleansers and body wash together and is explicitly wider than bath & shower proper - the MFDS release's own narrower '목욕용 제품류' (bath preparations) line is only KRW 130bn (2024), far smaller. These three readings should not be reconciled into one figure; they measure different things. The export figure (US$0.59bn, 2025, EXPORT_FOB, HIGH, MFDS via Yonhap/Korea Herald, 'body cleansing products') is unchanged and remains the only trade-flow figure. Two growth reads now exist, on different bases: a PRODUCTION-basis +9.88% YoY for 2024 (ESTIMATE confidence, derived from two adjacent years in the same MFDS annex table for the wider 인체 세정용 type - factory-gate output, not retail demand), and a LOW-confidence RETAIL forecast of 2.10% CAGR (2026-2035, Expert Market Research) on the narrower bath-products scope. The gap between a high-single-digit production read and a low-single-digit retail forecast is consistent with the two describing different scopes and different bases, not a contradiction to resolve. None of the three size figures share a scope: EMR's bath-products retail figure, the MFDS wider cleansing-type production figure, and the MFDS narrower bath-preparations line are three different measures of overlapping-but-distinct things. The +9.88% growth figure is PRODUCTION basis (factory-gate, ESTIMATE confidence) and should not be read as retail demand growth.

passages.title: Analyst read — bath shower (India)
passages.text: India's bath & shower segment now has data, but its own two IMARC figures are internally impossible: IMARC's 'bath & shower products' total (US$1.8bn, 2025, RETAIL, LOW), which IMARC itself says includes bath soap, is smaller than IMARC's own separate 'bath soap' figure for the same year (US$3,406.3mn, 2025, RETAIL, LOW) - a component reading 1.9x larger than the whole it is supposed to sit inside. MarkNtel's independent bath-soap-only figure (US$3.54bn, 2024, RETAIL, LOW) corroborates IMARC's soap figure within about 4%, reinforcing that IMARC's 'wider category' total is the outlier, not the soap figures. No organised-vs-unorganised coverage is stated by any of the three sources. Forecast CAGRs mirror the same split: IMARC's bath-and-shower total forecasts 3.80% (2026-2034, LOW) while IMARC's own bath-soap-only figure forecasts a faster 4.88% over the identical window, and MarkNtel's bath-soap CAGR is 3.16% (2025-2030, LOW). No growth_yoy figure exists for India bath & shower - this remains an open research gap (three separate research attempts, including a company-results sweep, did not find a defensible single-year observed rate). The IMARC 'bath & shower products' total should be treated with real caution given it is smaller than its own stated bath-soap-alone subset - a mathematical impossibility, not just a definitional gap. The two corroborating bath-soap-only figures (IMARC, MarkNtel) are the better-supported anchor for that narrower slice, but a clean 'whole bath & shower category' figure (soap + wash + additives) does not currently exist on file. growth_yoy remains a standing gap.

passages.title: Analyst read — bath shower (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Korea has one LOW-confidence RETAIL size read for bath & shower (US$357.35mn, 2025, narrower 'bath products' scope) and a separate HIGH-confidence EXPORT_FOB figure (US$0.59bn, 2025). India has three RETAIL candidates that do not reconcile with each other (US$1.8bn total that is internally contradicted by its own US$3,406.3mn bath-soap component, plus a corroborating US$3.54bn bath-soap-only MarkNtel figure), so there is no single India value_usd_bn clean enough to set against Korea's figure - a KR-vs-IN size comparison is not attempted here. Bath & shower is not one of the segments flagged as corridor-relevant in config/corridor.yaml (that list covers skincare, sun_care, colour_cosmetics, hair_care, and dermocosmetics), and no data point on either side carries a [CORRIDOR] tag, so no K-beauty-in-India read applies to this segment.

passages.title: Analyst read — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's colour cosmetics now has both a domestic anchor and a trade figure, on three distinct bases that must not be conflated. Domestic production (MFDS via Personal Care Insights/REACH24H) is KRW 2.68tn in 2024 and KRW 2.84tn in 2025 (MEDIUM, PRODUCTION basis) — roughly 15-16% of Korea's total cosmetics output. Retail-basis market sizes are two conflicting LOW aggregator estimates (Expert Market Research US$2.86bn 2025 vs Market Research Future US$2.22bn 2024). Exports are US$1.51bn (2025, EXPORT_FOB, HIGH, MFDS via Yonhap). Production growth was a striking +51.4% YoY in 2024 (MEDIUM, PRODUCTION) — an output surge, not necessarily domestic demand — moderating to lipstick/liner production +13.5% in 2025. Exports grew +12% YoY 2025 (HIGH). Retail forecast CAGRs are 5.9-6.2% (LOW). Production, export, and retail growth measure different things and should be read separately. The strongest figure is production (MEDIUM), which is factory-gate output — inflated by Korea's export-manufacturing role, not a home-demand read; the two retail estimates are LOW and modestly conflicting; exports are a separate EXPORT_FOB measure.

passages.title: Analyst read — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: India's colour_cosmetics market size is put at US$3.46bn for 2024 (RETAIL/MRP-inclusive basis, LOW confidence, source DMI). A separate figure puts the mass tier at 79.55% of colour_cosmetics market share for 2025 (RETAIL basis, LOW confidence, Mordor Intelligence), suggesting the segment is currently mass-tier dominated by this estimate. New sub-segment sizings (face_makeup ~US$1.89bn, lip_colour ~US$1.39bn, nail ~US$0.83bn, 2024, MRFF LOW) now give a rough internal breakdown. A growth_yoy figure now exists but is not an independent observed rate: derived from two consecutive Market Research Future values (US$5.55bn 2024 to US$5.89bn 2025), it works out to +6.13% (ESTIMATE confidence) — essentially the same number as MRF's own 6.18% forecast CAGR, since the 2025 value is modelled off that CAGR rather than separately observed. No independently-observed growth_yoy exists for India colour_cosmetics. Forecast CAGRs from other sources span 6.18-8.41% (LOW), and a lipstick-only sub read shows ~9.6% CAGR (TechSci/Markets and Data) — all forward-looking, not observed growth. India figures are LOW-confidence aggregator estimates; the segment total and the sub-segment splits come from different houses on different definitions, so the parts will not sum cleanly to the whole, and organised-vs-unorganised coverage is unstated.

passages.title: Analyst read — colour cosmetics (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both geographies now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn figures, so a directional comparison is possible: India (~US$3.46bn, LOW) is larger than Korea's retail colour cosmetics (~US$2.2-2.9bn, LOW), though every figure here is LOW confidence. The sharper contrast is structural — Korea's production (KRW 2.68tn, ~15% of national cosmetics output) reflects its role as a global colour-cosmetics manufacturing hub feeding US$1.51bn of exports, whereas India's number is a home-demand retail estimate. On the corridor, colour cosmetics shows real if unquantified K-beauty pull (Hince via Tira Jan-2026, Etude tints on Blinkit), but no [CORRIDOR]-tagged market figure exists yet.

passages.title: Analyst read — deodorants (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's deodorants segment now has data, though the size read is dated: a MEDIUM-confidence Euromonitor-via-Pharm-News figure puts the domestic RETAIL market at KRW 63.7bn in 2018 (~US$43.1mn), the most recent Korean-language figure that could be verified on a fetched page. A separate LOW-confidence figure from Actual Market Research states the market was 'more than' US$160mn in 2023 - a floor, not a point estimate, and roughly 3.7x the 2018 figure on a USD basis with no stated definitional change, so the two should not be averaged. A HIGH-confidence Euromonitor figure also shows the category is highly concentrated: Beiersdorf Korea (Nivea) holds a 'commanding' 59% share in 2025, though the underlying value figures behind that share are paywalled. The only growth figure is also 2018-vintage: +7.0% (MEDIUM confidence, Euromonitor-via-Pharm-News, domestic RETAIL, KRW terms). No forecast CAGR could be found on any fetchable page for this segment - a Statista Consumer Market Outlook page and a Sphericalinsights page were checked but returned unusable (paywalled/unreachable) content, so this remains an open research gap. The only sourced size and growth figures for this segment are both 2018-vintage; treat the market as stale-dated rather than current. The 2023 Actual Market Research figure is stated as a floor ('more than US$160mn') and its scope may include antiperspirant/body-mist adjacencies not covered by the 2018 figure, so the two should not be read as a continuous series. cagr_forecast remains a standing gap for Korea.

passages.title: Analyst read — deodorants (India)
passages.text: India's deodorants segment now has a RETAIL size read: US$1.0bn (2025, LOW confidence, IMARC Group, rounded to one decimal by the source). A MEDIUM-confidence company proxy also exists: Vini Cosmetics (maker of Fogg, India's largest deodorant brand by volume share) reported revenue growth of 17% for the year ending March 2025 (FY25, NET_REALISATION basis, sourced from Tracxn's MCA/ROC-filing-based profile) - a company figure, not a category-wide market growth rate, used because no brand-level or category-wide growth figure could be found for the larger diversified players (HUL, Godrej, ITC) where deodorants is one line among many. A similarly-sourced proxy for McNroe Consumer Products (Wild Stone, the #2 deodorant maker) shows a directionally consistent 20% figure for the same period, though this is noted for context rather than recorded as an independent claim. Three forecast CAGRs exist on essentially the same product scope (sprays, roll-ons, creams, gels, sticks, wipes) and span a wide 3.10-9.13% range: IMARC 3.10% (2026-2034, LOW), Expert Market Research 7.80% (2026-2035, LOW), and Bonafide Research 9.13% (2024-2029, LOW) - a roughly 3x spread between the extremes that the sources do not reconcile. The Vini Cosmetics 17% figure is the only observed year-on-year read, and it is company-level, not a category rate. The three forecast CAGRs disagree by up to 3x on effectively the same scope and should not be averaged. The Vini Cosmetics growth figure is a single company (India's #1 deodorant brand by volume) standing in for the category because no category-wide or diversified-player figure could be sourced; organised-market only, with no unorganised-market read implied. Organised-vs-unorganised coverage is not stated by any of the three forecast sources.

passages.title: Analyst read — deodorants (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both geographies now carry a RETAIL market-size figure, but neither is on solid footing for a direct comparison: Korea's is 2018-vintage (KRW 63.7bn, ~US$43.1mn) alongside a 2023 floor-only figure (>US$160mn) that may cover a different scope, while India's (US$1.0bn, 2025) is a single current-year LOW-confidence read. Given Korea's most defensible figure is seven years stale, a same-period KR-vs-IN size comparison is not attempted here. No [CORRIDOR]-tagged data point exists for deodorants in either file, and deodorants is not among the segments flagged as corridor-relevant in config/corridor.yaml.

passages.title: Analyst read — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's dermocosmetics segment now has a size anchor, but the Korean sources disagree sharply. Samjong KPMG (via Korea Herald) puts the market at KRW 4.5tn in 2020 (MEDIUM, RETAIL); the Korean Enterprise Reputation Research body also cites KRW 4.5tn but for 2022, with KRW 5.5tn projected for 2025; and a cosmeceutical institute gives a much lower KRW 1.2tn for 2020. That is a definitional tangle — 'dermocosmetics/cosmeceutical' is drawn differently by each — so the figure is anchored around the low-single-digit KRW-trillions but not pinned. Euromonitor's HIGH-confidence +13% YoY growth (2024) still stands as the most reliable single datapoint. Euromonitor reports +13% YoY for 2024 (HIGH, RETAIL), driven by actives (PDRN, exosomes, peptides) — the segment is growing fast. A forward CAGR now exists where none did before: derived from the KERI series itself (KRW 4.5325tn actual 2022 to KRW 5.5tn projected 2025), the implied rate is 6.66% (ESTIMATE, a floor since the 2025 figure is itself stated as a floor), corroborated by an independently-sourced SPER Market Research estimate of 5.45% (2024-2033, LOW — though SPER's own companion market-size figure of US$27.89bn by 2033 is not credible, since it would exceed Korea's entire domestic BPC market, and is not claimed). A separate derived historical CAGR of 55.4% (2017-2022, ESTIMATE) captures the category's explosive early formation off a tiny KRW 0.5tn (2017) base; the sharp deceleration from ~55% historical to ~5-7% forecast marks a shift from formation-phase to maturity, though the 2017 base may itself be understated given how much Korean sources disagree on the dermocosmetics definition. The size figures conflict by up to ~4x depending on how 'dermocosmetics' is scoped, and several are recorded on an NA basis because the source definition was unclear — treat scale as indicative; the growth read (Euromonitor, HIGH) is the firmer signal. The new forward CAGRs (6.66%, 5.45%) are both derived/estimated rather than a single published forecast rate, so read them as an order-of-magnitude signal (mid-single-digit forward growth), not a precise number.

passages.title: Analyst read — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: India dermocosmetics is anchored by P&S Market Research at US$0.28bn (2024, RETAIL, LOW) — but that is a narrow, Rx-adjacent definition (US$256mn 2023 base, ~10.3% CAGR to US$505mn 2030). A much broader competing estimate (MarkWide US$1.85bn 2026, ~11.6% CAGR) is roughly 7x larger, a pure definitional gap. A masstige-tier-only cut (Expert Market Research US$65.55mn 2025, 14.6% CAGR) sits below both. Derma-D2C revenue is now on file too (Minimalist Rs347cr FY24, NET_REALISATION). All reads point to fast growth — forecast CAGRs span ~10% (P&S, narrow) to ~15% (EMR, masstige) — but every one is a LOW-confidence forecast, not observed growth. Minimalist's Rs184cr (FY23) to Rs347cr (FY24) revenue jump is a single-company signal, not the segment's rate. The ~7x spread between the narrow (P&S) and broad (MarkWide) sizings means India dermocosmetics scale is genuinely unresolved in the data; all sources are LOW confidence with differing organised/Rx scope.

passages.title: Analyst read — dermocosmetics (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both sides now carry a value_usd_bn size, so a rough comparison is possible — Korea (KRW ~4.5tn ≈ US$3bn, MEDIUM) is an order of magnitude larger than India's narrow US$0.28bn read, and still larger than India's broad US$1.85bn read — but both sides are definitionally unstable (KR sources ~4x apart, IN sources ~7x apart), so this is directional, not a firm ratio. The more decision-relevant fact is momentum plus corridor fit: both markets are growing double-digit, and dermocosmetics is the corridor's highest-conviction whitespace (mid-price derma K-beauty in Tier 2/3). Fresh corridor evidence — Nykaa's K-beauty GMV +60% YoY (Q3 2025), Medicube/Illiyoon/Aestura launching on Nykaa/Tira through 2026 — confirms the pull, though no India brand-level K-derma revenue is published yet.

passages.title: Analyst read — emerging adjacencies (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's emerging adjacencies now has data for two of six taxonomy sub-segments. Beauty_devices: US$1.32bn (2024, RETAIL, LOW confidence, Expert Market Research), a home/consumer device scope (acne, hair-removal, cleansing, oxygen/steamer, rejuvenation devices) that may overlap professional aesthetic devices; this is a sub-segment figure only, not a segment total. Ingestible_nutricosmetics: ~KRW 1.0tn in 2023 (~US$0.676bn, RETAIL, MEDIUM confidence, Shinhan Financial Investment Research via Seoul Finance), up from ~KRW 0.7tn in 2019 - though this 'inner beauty' market is sold as health-functional food in Korea, so it sits outside the conventional BPC retail perimeter and should not be added to BPC totals without flagging that risk. The other four sub-segments (halal_certified, ayurvedic_herbal, clean_vegan, kbeauty_derivative) have no Korea data. Beauty_devices carries the fastest verified KR adjacency growth: a LOW-confidence 13.8% CAGR (2025-2034, Expert Market Research) - roughly 2.5x the pace of KR skincare or hair care - plus a MEDIUM-confidence company-level proxy of +44.6% YoY for 2024 (APR Corp's AGE-R brand, NET_REALISATION basis, company earnings announcement), used because no clean same-source category-wide two-year series could be found; APR is Korea's largest listed home beauty-device player, so this is a leading-indicator proxy, not a market-wide rate. Ingestible_nutricosmetics shows a historical +9.3% CAGR (2019-2023, ESTIMATE, derived from two endpoints on the same source) against a much more aggressive company projection of KRW 2.0tn by 2025 (MEDIUM confidence, same source) that would imply roughly 41% CAGR from 2023 - a projection well above the observed historical trend, not (yet) an outturn. Both sub-segment growth figures for beauty_devices are proxies (a forecast CAGR and a single company's revenue growth), not an observed category-wide rate. The nutricosmetics 2025 projection (KRW 2.0tn) is a sell-side forecast from 2024 that implies a sharp acceleration off the observed 2019-2023 trend and has no verified 2025 outturn on file. Four of six taxonomy sub-segments remain entirely without Korea data.

passages.title: Analyst read — emerging adjacencies (India)
passages.text: India's emerging adjacencies now has data across five of six taxonomy sub-segments. Ayurvedic_herbal: the cleanest BPC-scoped figure is IMARC's ayurvedic-skincare-only read at US$2.0bn (2025, RETAIL, LOW) - this excludes ayurvedic oral care and colour cosmetics, so it under-covers the adjacency; a wider, ESTIMATE-confidence derived figure of INR 42,735cr (~2.2x the skincare-only figure) covers skin, oral, hair and fragrances, with the same publisher's organised/unorganised split (70%/30%, 2025) applied. Halal_certified: US$1.3bn (2025, RETAIL, LOW, IMARC), organised/unorganised coverage not stated, and the category is inherently hard to audit since halal certification in India has no single national register. Clean_vegan: INR 7,786.49cr (~US$0.81bn, 2025, RETAIL, LOW, Expert Market Research), a publisher-defined 'clean' boundary with no Indian regulatory basis. Beauty_devices: two closely-agreeing LOW-confidence figures on an identical personal-care-appliance scope (trimmers, dryers, straighteners, epilators) - IMARC US$2.1bn (2025) and TechSci US$1.81bn (2024) - unusually consistent for a pair of aggregators, though this is a grooming-appliance basket, not the at-home skincare-device (LED mask, microcurrent) reading the taxonomy targets. Kbeauty_derivative [CORRIDOR]: two LOW-confidence figures directly contradict each other - MarkNtel US$310mn for 2025 versus Credence Research's higher US$406.58mn for the earlier year 2023, an outright contradiction on a category both describe as growing. Growth reads vary sharply by sub-segment and scope. Ayurvedic: skincare-only forecasts 11.98% (2026-2034, LOW, IMARC) while the wider personal-care-plus-non-BPC-healthcare basket forecasts 15.52% (2026-2034, LOW) - the latter is 58% healthcare/medicine by the source's own breakdown and should not be applied to the BPC adjacency. Halal: 7.28% (2026-2034, LOW, IMARC); a MarkNtel figure reportedly near 30% could not be verified on a fetched page and is not recorded. Clean_vegan carries both a forecast (15.7% CAGR, 2026-2035, LOW) and an observed company read: Honasa Consumer (Mamaearth) reported 20% YoY revenue growth for FY26 (HIGH confidence, BSE regulatory filing) - company-level across Honasa's full portfolio, not a category-wide clean/vegan market rate, since no market-wide series exists. Beauty_devices CAGRs also agree closely (14.56% IMARC vs 15.56% TechSci, both LOW). Kbeauty_derivative CAGRs diverge on top of the size contradiction: 18.06% (MarkNtel) vs 10.00% (Credence Research), both LOW, both [CORRIDOR]-tagged. The ayurvedic wider-basket growth rate (15.52%) is majority non-BPC and must not be quoted as a BPC growth figure. The kbeauty_derivative pair is a genuine contradiction, not just a gap - a later year reading lower than an earlier year on a category both sources describe as growing - so neither figure should be treated as settled; grey-market/parallel-import K-beauty is a known unmeasured channel that likely means both undercount actual sell-through. The Honasa 20% figure is a diversified-portfolio company result (Mamaearth plus six other brands, some dermatology-positioned rather than clean/vegan) standing in for a sub-segment with no market-wide series. Organised/unorganised coverage is stated only for the wider ayurvedic estimate (70%/30%); it is unstated elsewhere.

passages.title: Analyst read — emerging adjacencies (Korea vs India)
passages.text: A KR-vs-IN comparison is only possible sub-segment by sub-segment, and even then is limited: beauty_devices is the one sub-segment with a size figure on both sides, but the scopes differ (Korea: home devices including oxygen/steamer/rejuvenation; India: personal-care grooming appliances including trimmers and hair dryers), so a direct value_usd_bn comparison would compare different baskets, not the same market. Kbeauty_derivative is [CORRIDOR]-tagged in India (US$310-407mn, contradictory across two sources) with no Korea-side counterpart figure recorded for this specific sub-segment. No other sub-segment has data on both sides. Given the scope mismatches and one-sided coverage, no aggregate KR-vs-IN emerging-adjacencies comparison is attempted here.

passages.title: Analyst read — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's fragrances segment now has domestic size and production data, not just exports, though the aggregator readings disagree sharply. Two LOW-confidence RETAIL 'perfume' market-size figures for the identical year 2025 conflict: IMARC US$792.5mn versus Expert Market Research US$485.19mn, a 1.63x gap that scope alone does not explain (EMR's stated scope, 'fragrances and perfume', is wider than IMARC's 'perfume', yet EMR's number is smaller) - neither is a headline figure without a Euromonitor or MFDS/KOSIS cross-check. A HIGH-confidence MFDS PRODUCTION figure also exists: KRW 68.0bn (2024, ~US$46.0mn) for the '방향용' (fragrance) cosmetics-registered product type - about 17x smaller than IMARC's retail figure, which reflects both the basis difference (factory-gate vs retail) and that MFDS excludes imported fragrance in an import-dominated Korean market, not a conflict to reconcile. Export figures (US$0.06bn 2025 EXPORT_FOB HIGH; US$0.039471bn 2024 world HS3303 HIGH) are unchanged, with a negligible [CORRIDOR]-tagged US$6,000 flow to India in 2024. A PRODUCTION-basis growth figure now exists: +14.67% YoY for 2024 (ESTIMATE confidence, derived from two adjacent years in the same MFDS annex table) - domestic manufacturing growth only, excluding imports, and notably slower than the +20.9% all-cosmetics production growth over the same period. Three forecast CAGRs disagree on both level and pace: IMARC 4.62% (2026-2034, LOW), Expert Market Research 6.30% (2026-2035, LOW, ~36% faster than IMARC), and SPER Market Research 5.2% (2023-2028, LOW) - a roughly 2.5x dispersion in the underlying market-size levels these three aggregators imply, which is why no single Korea fragrance market size is presented as a headline figure. The export-side +46.2% YoY note for 2025 (HIGH confidence) remains the most reliable growth signal, though it describes trade flow, not domestic demand. SPER's page contains an internally impossible trajectory (a stated 2022 level and 2033 endpoint inconsistent with its own claimed CAGR) - only its CAGR is recorded, not its size figures. The two RETAIL market-size aggregators disagree 1.63x with no scope explanation, and the MFDS production figure measures a different, narrower, domestic-only base - none of the three should be combined or averaged.

passages.title: Analyst read — fragrances (India)
passages.text: India fragrances has two RETAIL market-size estimates, both LOW confidence: US$2.6bn (2024) covering perfume plus deodorant combined, and a narrower US$0.281bn (FY24) covering perfume only - different scope, so not directly comparable to each other. Import data is HIGH confidence: India imported US$0.331681bn of fragrances (HS 3303) from the world in 2024, with Korea (US$0.000135bn, [CORRIDOR]-tagged) and China (US$0.000249bn) each a minor source. An ESTIMATE-confidence import-dependence figure of 12.8% notes that premium fragrance is import-reliant (UAE the largest source, then France) while mass-market perfume/deodorant is largely made domestically. A HIGH-confidence company figure now exists alongside these: Titan Company's Fragrances division (SKINN and Fastrack Perfumes brands) grew approximately 26% YoY in Q4FY25 (NET_REALISATION basis, BSE/NSE regulatory filing) - company-level, not a category-wide market figure, and Titan does not separately disclose Fragrances' absolute revenue. The Vini Cosmetics/Fogg company figure (FY25 revenue INR 1200cr, NET_REALISATION, MEDIUM confidence) reflects one company's deodorant business, not the fragrances segment as a whole. Formal forecast CAGRs now exist alongside the informal figures embedded in the market-size notes. On the perfume-only scope (the closest match to the taxonomy segment): IMARC 5.36% (2026-2034, LOW). On the wider perfume-plus-deodorant scope: IMARC 10.26% (2026-2034, LOW) and TechSci 11.54% (2025-2030, LOW) on differing size bases roughly 1.9x apart - deodorants roughly double both the base and the growth rate, so the perfume-only and perfume-plus-deodorant readings are not substitutes for each other. The market-size claims' own notes separately carry two older, informal CAGRs (roughly 11.1% for the perfume+deodorant estimate, 15.23% for the perfume-only estimate) that predate these formal IMARC/TechSci figures and are not independently corroborated forecasts in their own right. Titan's ~26% Q4FY25 figure is the only observed year-on-year read, and it is company-level, not a category rate. Five different growth-rate readings now exist for India fragrances across two scope definitions (perfume-only vs perfume-plus-deodorant) and should not be blended into one number. The 12.8% import-dependence figure is itself labelled ESTIMATE/derived rather than a directly sourced number. Titan's growth figure reflects one company's two-brand division within a larger 'Emerging Businesses' segment, not the category.

passages.title: Analyst read — fragrances (Korea vs India)
passages.text: A like-for-like comparison of Korea and India fragrances remains difficult even with fuller data on both sides: Korea's RETAIL market-size aggregators disagree 1.63x (US$792.5mn vs US$485.19mn, both 2025) and India's disagree by scope (US$2.6bn perfume+deodorant vs US$0.281bn perfume-only), so neither geography has one settled value_usd_bn to set against the other. The Korea-to-India corridor trade flow is present but tiny on both sides of the ledger (KR exports to India US$6,000 in 2024; India imports from Korea US$135,000 in 2024, both [CORRIDOR]-tagged), suggesting fragrances remains a minor thread of the broader K-beauty corridor relative to categories like skincare.

passages.title: Analyst read — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's hair care now has a domestic size anchor: IMARC puts the market at US$1.8bn for 2025 (RETAIL, LOW confidence), forecast to US$2.4bn by 2034. That sits alongside the existing trade picture — total Korean hair-care exports (HS 3305) of US$0.413bn (EXPORT_FOB, HIGH, UN Comtrade, 2024), of which US$0.003bn went to India ([CORRIDOR]-tagged). A growth_yoy figure now exists but is a projection, not an observed rate: derived from two adjacent Mordor Intelligence forecast values (US$1.32bn 2025 to US$1.39bn 2026), it works out to +5.3% (ESTIMATE confidence) — consistent with the same source's own 5.42% CAGR (2026-2031) and roughly 2pp hotter than IMARC's separate forecast CAGR of 3.23% (2026-2034, LOW), which also disagrees with Mordor on level (a 1.36x gap). No observed KR growth_yoy is on file for the domestic market; the reliable observed figures remain on the export side. The domestic size is a single LOW-confidence aggregator estimate; the HIGH-confidence figures are exports (EXPORT_FOB), a different basis that cannot substitute for domestic retail scale.

passages.title: Analyst read — hair care (India)
passages.text: India's hair-care market is sized at US$4.1bn (RETAIL/MRP-inclusive, LOW, Mordor, 2026), with a 'skinification' shift toward actives and serums. Sub-segment detail is now firmer: shampoo ~US$1.26bn (2025), and scalp_care captured through three conflicting proxy measures (alopecia US$267mn, hair serum US$155mn, hair-growth products US$825mn) that reflect how differently 'scalp care' is scoped. India also imported US$0.199bn of hair-care products from the world (US$0.031bn from China) (IMPORT_CIF, HIGH, UN Comtrade, 2024). A growth_yoy figure now exists but is not independently observed: derived from two consecutive Market Research Future values (US$4,100mn 2024 to US$4,287.37mn 2025), it works out to +4.57% (ESTIMATE confidence) — numerically identical to MRF's own 4.57% forecast CAGR on the same page, since the 2025 value is modelled off that rate rather than separately measured. A forecast CAGR of 4.73% (2026-2031, LOW, Mordor) sits close to it, while IMARC's separate 10.58% (2026-2034, LOW) implies a much faster trajectory on the same market — none of these is an observed rate. The scalp-care/serum sub-space is where the 'skinification' momentum sits, but its size proxies are LOW and definitionally scattered. Segment and sub-segment figures are LOW-confidence aggregator estimates from different houses on different definitions; the three scalp-care measures are not comparable to each other, and organised/unorganised coverage is unstated.

passages.title: Analyst read — hair care (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both markets now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn sizes, so a directional comparison holds: India (~US$4.1bn, LOW) is roughly 2x Korea's domestic hair care (~US$1.8bn, LOW), though both are single LOW-confidence estimates. The corridor angle is thin in absolute terms — Korea's hair-care exports to India are just US$0.003bn ([CORRIDOR]), consistent with AmorePacific's Mise En Scène and RYO being recent (2025) Nykaa entrants rather than established sellers — while India separately imports US$0.199bn of hair care from the world (IMPORT_CIF, a different basis, not netted). The shared structural story is 'skinification': actives-led scalp/serum demand is the growth edge in both markets, and the clearest near-term corridor opportunity.

passages.title: Analyst read — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's men's grooming segment retains its Euromonitor anchor, though a new same-institution figure now conflicts with it: Euromonitor-via-Korea-Herald puts men's cosmetics at KRW 1.16tn (~US$0.78bn) for CY2025, MEDIUM confidence, RETAIL basis, while a separately-sourced Euromonitor-via-AMPM figure puts 2024 at KRW 1.2tn (~US$0.81bn) — a higher value for an earlier year from what appears to be the same underlying series, an unreconciled internal contradiction (one vintage is likely misdated or the category was rebased); do not build a growth rate across the two. A separate Future Market Insights estimate puts men's SKINCARE alone at US$1.2bn (2025, LOW) — still implausibly exceeding the whole men's-cosmetics figure, the same definitional mismatch as before. A cleaner same-series growth read is now available: Euromonitor-via-Jangup-Shinmun figures for 2020-2022 (KRW 1.064tn to 1.0751tn to 1.0923tn) imply +1.04% (2021) and +1.6% (2022) YoY (both ESTIMATE confidence, derived) — the 2022 figure cross-validates the KRW 1.09tn (2022) point already on file, confirming the series. The substantive finding: Korean domestic men's cosmetics is growing only around 1-2%/year in nominal KRW (flat-to-negative in real terms against Korean CPI) — well below both the 'booming K-male grooming' narrative and Future Market Insights' 11.04% CAGR forecast (2025-2035, LOW, on the men's-skincare-only basket, not the whole segment). The one reasonably-solid figure (Euromonitor, MEDIUM) covers 'men's cosmetics', but two Euromonitor-attributed vintages now conflict (KRW 1.16tn for 2025 vs KRW 1.2tn for 2024) and are not reconciled, so absolute scale should be read as anchored in the low-single-digit KRW trillions but not pinned to either exact figure; the LOW FMI figure uses a broader, internally-inconsistent skincare basket that exceeds both. The firmer signal is the ~1-2%/year nominal growth rate (ESTIMATE, derived from a consistent 2020-2022 series).

passages.title: Analyst read — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: India men's grooming is the better-evidenced side: Euromonitor sizes it at INR 186.3bn (~US$1.94bn) for 2025, HIGH confidence, RETAIL, growing +9% YoY (also HIGH). IBEF frames the trajectory as INR 20,500cr (2024) to INR 38,300cr (2033), MEDIUM. The men's_skincare sub-segment — corridor whitespace #4 — sizes ~US$1.02bn (Deep Market Insights, LOW). Several LOW aggregator whole-segment estimates cluster US$2.3-2.45bn on differing 'male grooming' baskets. Observed +9% YoY for 2025 (HIGH, Euromonitor). Forecast CAGRs span 5-12% (LOW-MEDIUM) depending on basket; IBEF's 2024-2033 path implies roughly 7%. Men's skincare is repeatedly cited as the fastest-growing slice, consistent with the whitespace read, though the sub-segment growth figures themselves are LOW. Only the Euromonitor size and growth are HIGH confidence; the aggregator estimates vary materially in scope (men's cosmetics vs 'male grooming products' vs razors-inclusive), so they corroborate direction, not a precise number.

passages.title: Analyst read — mens grooming (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both sides now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn figures, so a directional comparison holds: India (~US$1.94bn, HIGH, 2025) is roughly 2.5x the size of Korea's men's cosmetics (~US$0.78bn, MEDIUM, 2025) in absolute terms and is far better evidenced. The confidence gap matters — India's figure is Euromonitor-HIGH, Korea's is Euromonitor-MEDIUM via press — so treat the ratio as directional. Korea's distinction is intensity, not size: it is the world's highest per-capita men's beauty market, whereas India is the larger absolute opportunity with men's skincare flagged as corridor whitespace. No K-beauty men's-grooming-in-India market figure surfaced in research, so the corridor angle here stays qualitative.

passages.title: Analyst read — oral care (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's oral_care segment now has domestic size data, not just trade flow, though the two RETAIL aggregator figures run in the wrong direction relative to each other: Grand View Research (via Daxue Consulting) puts the market at US$975.9mn for 2024, while Deep Market Insights puts a LATER year, 2025, at a LOWER US$892.82mn - roughly 1.19x apart once normal growth is allowed for, an unresolved definitional mismatch (both LOW confidence, neither states channel coverage or duty-free treatment). A MEDIUM-confidence MFDS PRODUCTION figure also exists, but narrowly scoped: KRW 405.1bn (2024, ~US$274.0mn) for 치약제 (dentifrice/toothpaste) only, since Korea regulates toothpaste as a quasi-drug rather than a cosmetic - this excludes toothbrushes, mouthwash and other formats, so it is well short of a full oral-care read; it is roughly 1.5x below Daxue/Grand View's retail figure, consistent with a retail-vs-production and import-coverage difference, not a conflict. Export figures are unchanged: US$0.079986bn HS3306 world exports (2024, HIGH), of which US$0.000251bn ([CORRIDOR]-tagged) went to India. The two RETAIL forecast CAGRs agree closely despite disagreeing on level: Grand View/Daxue 6.9% (2025-2030, LOW) versus Deep Market Insights 6.41% (2026-2034, LOW), within about half a point of each other. Against that, a PRODUCTION-basis growth figure shows the opposite direction: Korean domestic toothpaste production FELL 3.27% in 2024 (ESTIMATE confidence, derived from two consecutive MFDS quasi-drug statistics releases) - a genuine contrary signal, flagged deliberately rather than smoothed over. Production and retail are different measures (factory-gate dentifrice-only output vs. retail sell-through across the whole category including imports), so a production decline alongside forecast retail growth is not a contradiction to resolve, though it may point to import substitution or a mix shift away from dentifrice - a hypothesis, not a settled finding. Do not read the -3.27% production figure as 'the' Korea oral care growth rate: it covers dentifrice production only and excludes imports, while the two positive forecast CAGRs describe retail demand across a wider category. The two RETAIL size figures disagree in the wrong direction (later year, lower level) and should not be averaged.

passages.title: Analyst read — oral care (India)
passages.text: India oral_care now has multiple RETAIL size reads that disagree, plus one that revised itself. IMARC: US$1.1bn (2025, LOW). The India Watch: INR 21,000cr (~US$2.18bn, 2025, LOW, trade publication with no disclosed methodology) - about 2.0x IMARC's figure for the same year. Renub Research: US$2.03bn (2024, LOW) in an earlier report, but the same publisher's later report page gives US$1.23bn (2025, LOW) - a roughly 40% downward revision with no stated definitional change; the later Renub figure sits closer to IMARC, the earlier one closer to The India Watch. A HIGH-confidence company figure now exists alongside these: Dabur India's Oral Care business declined 5.2% YoY in FY25 (RETAIL basis, secondary-sales/sell-through, BSE regulatory filing) - company-level, not the category, and the company's own investor deck attributes the decline to a high base effect (Q4FY24 oral care had grown 22% YoY); for context, Dabur's oral care business had grown 5.3% YoY in the prior quarter (Q2FY25), so this is not read as a sustained category downturn. Three forecast CAGRs cluster more tightly than the size figures: IMARC 4.15% (2026-2034, LOW), Renub's earlier vintage 5.18% (2025-2033, LOW, off the US$2.03bn base), and Renub's later vintage 4.45% (2026-2034, LOW, off the US$1.23bn base) - the rates agree far better than the levels do. Dabur's -5.2% is the only observed year-on-year figure and is company-specific, explicitly attributed by the company to a prior-year high base rather than a category-wide slowdown. Renub Research revised its own India oral care size down about 40% between two published vintages with no stated definitional change - a publisher reliability signal, not just an ordinary cross-source gap. Dabur's -5.2% should not be read as a category-wide contraction: it is one company's branded secondary sales, explicitly base-effect-driven per the company's own commentary, and organised-market only.

passages.title: Analyst read — oral care (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both geographies now carry RETAIL size figures, but neither has one that is internally settled: Korea's two aggregator figures disagree by direction (a later year reading lower), and India's range from US$1.1bn to US$2.18bn across three sources, one of which revised itself ~40% between vintages. Given neither side offers a single defensible value_usd_bn, no KR-vs-IN size comparison is attempted here. The two [CORRIDOR]-tagged trade figures - Korea's ~US$0.000251bn FOB export to India versus India's ~US$0.000485bn CIF import from Korea - describe the same HS 3306 flow from opposite customs sides; the difference likely reflects the FOB/CIF basis gap and normal mirror-statistics discrepancy rather than two distinct quantities.

passages.title: Analyst read — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Two distinct measures exist for Korea skincare and should not be summed: a HIGH-confidence domestic retail market size of KRW 7.653tn (~US$5.18bn equivalent, 2025, Euromonitor) and a HIGH-confidence export figure of US$8.54bn (EXPORT_FOB, 2025, ~75% of Korea's total cosmetics exports, MFDS). The export number is larger than the retail number because they measure different things (overseas sales vs. domestic sell-through), not because exports exceed the home market. Separate UN Comtrade HS 3304 data show Korea exported US$8.567bn to the world in 2024 (EXPORT_FOB) but only US$0.0656bn of that went to India [CORRIDOR]; HS 3304 also blends makeup with skincare, so this is not a skincare-only cut. Korea skincare also now has its first primary sub-segment breakdown: MFDS 2024 production data (HIGH confidence, PRODUCTION basis) shows facial moisturisers (lotion/cream/essence/oil combined) at KRW 5,751.5bn, sheet/pack masks at KRW 1,316.9bn, and facial cleansers (foam cleanser plus other cleansing) at KRW 885.5bn — all factory-gate output including export-bound volume, not domestic retail. The moisturiser figure spans two taxonomy cells (facial_moisturisers and serums_ampoules combined) and must not be added to the separate LOW-confidence serums_ampoules or toners_essences retail estimates already on file, which are one to two orders of magnitude smaller — a basis-and-scope gap, not a conflict. Domestic retail grew a modest 1.0% YoY in 2025 (Euromonitor, RETAIL), while skincare-led exports grew 11.6% YoY in 2025 (MFDS, EXPORT_FOB) - two different bases moving at different speeds. A LOW-confidence forecast CAGR of 5.6% (2025-2034, Expert Market Research) is now on file for retail, though its companion size figure is not claimed here since it would create a >20% gap against the Euromonitor retail anchor. The new MFDS sub-segment production data shows sharp 2024 growth - facial moisturisers +29.52%, sheet/pack masks +33.45%, facial cleansers +30.03% (all ESTIMATE confidence, PRODUCTION basis) - but this is factory-gate output inflated by export-bound volume, not evidence of domestic demand growing at that rate. The retail and export figures are both HIGH confidence but sit on different value_basis (RETAIL vs EXPORT_FOB) and must never be netted; the Comtrade HS 3304 figures additionally mix makeup into the skincare total. The new sub-segment production figures (HIGH confidence) are wider than their taxonomy cells (the moisturiser figure includes essence/oil, the mask figure includes non-sheet formats) and are production-, not retail-, basis, so should not be read as domestic sub-segment retail sizes.

passages.title: Analyst read — skincare (India)
passages.text: India's skincare market is sized at US$9.06bn (2025, RETAIL, LOW confidence, IMARC) - LOW because it is an aggregator estimate rather than a primary source. Two market-share reads of skincare's weight in adjacent baskets diverge structurally rather than contradicting each other: IMARC puts skincare/sun care at 35% of total BPC, while Grand View Research puts skincare at 49% of a narrower "cosmetics" basket - different denominators, not comparable directly. HIGH-confidence UN Comtrade data show India importing US$0.844bn of HS 3304 goods (skincare plus makeup) from the world in 2024, of which US$0.140bn came from Korea specifically [CORRIDOR] and US$0.188bn from China; a separate ESTIMATE (not a primary figure, methodology shown) derives import dependence at 9.3%, implying roughly 91% of the market by value is domestically supplied. India skincare also now has sub-segment detail across serums/ampoules, sheet masks, facial cleansers, facial moisturisers, lip care, body care and hand care - all LOW-confidence aggregator estimates, several internally conflicting (e.g. sheet-mask-inclusive facial-mask totals span US$143-451mn 2024-2025 across two sources). One sub-segment gap remains standing on purpose: toners_essences has a country-level forecast CAGR (11.1%, 2026-2033, Persistence Market Research, naming India the fastest-growing toner market globally) but no market-size figure has been found for it. A growth_yoy figure now exists: Statista Market Insights puts India skin care revenue growth at 3.0% for 2026 (MEDIUM confidence) - though the same claim's own notes flag that Statista's forward CAGR on the same page is only 2.76% (2026-2031), far more conservative than IMARC's separate 7.49% CAGR-to-2034 (LOW) referenced in its own market-size notes, so the two should not be read together without normalising. A single-company data point (Minimalist, NET_REALISATION, MEDIUM confidence, FY24) shows revenue up from Rs184cr (FY23) to Rs347cr - one D2C brand's growth, not the market. Most India skincare figures here are LOW-confidence aggregator estimates (IMARC, Grand View Research, MarkNtel, IMA Pro) rather than primary-sourced, and none states organised-vs-unorganised coverage explicitly; several retail-price points are individual K-beauty SKUs [CORRIDOR], not market-wide figures.

passages.title: Analyst read — skincare (Korea vs India)
passages.text: A like-for-like size comparison is possible here because both sides carry a value_usd_bn figure on a RETAIL basis: Korea's domestic retail market converts to ~US$5.18bn (2025, HIGH confidence) versus India's ~US$9.06bn (2025, LOW confidence) - India reads larger on this comparison, though the confidence gap (HIGH vs LOW) means it should be treated as indicative, not precise. Korea's US$8.54bn EXPORT_FOB export figure sits on a different value_basis and cannot be netted against India's retail figure. The Korea-to-India corridor is real but small and inconsistent between reporting sides: Korea reports US$0.0656bn of HS 3304 (skincare plus makeup) exports to India in 2024 [CORRIDOR], while India reports US$0.140bn of HS 3304 imports from Korea in the same year [CORRIDOR] - a mismatch consistent with FOB-vs-CIF differences and mirror-trade-statistics discrepancies, and neither figure isolates skincare from makeup. A substantial set of individual K-beauty SKU retail prices captured from Nykaa and Blinkit (COSRX, Laneige, Innisfree, Anua, Beauty of Joseon, and others) document this corridor at the shelf level, but these are product-level price points, not a market-size figure for the corridor itself.

passages.title: Analyst read — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's sun-care segment now has a domestic anchor, but the cleanest figure is a production measure, not a retail one: MFDS sunscreen production value of KRW 0.47tn for CY2025 (MEDIUM confidence, PRODUCTION basis), which is factory-gate output and must not be read as domestic retail sell-through. Retail-basis market sizes are two conflicting LOW-confidence aggregator estimates — Grand View US$330mn (2024) versus MarkNtel US$747mn (2025), roughly a 2.3x spread. Reported SPF penetration is high but also conflicting (45% to 75%, both LOW). MFDS production grew +9.4% YoY in CY2025 (observed, MEDIUM, PRODUCTION basis). Forecast retail CAGRs sit between 3.59% (MarkNtel) and 8.3% (Grand View), both LOW. A separately reported +43% figure (Samsung Securities via Korea Herald) is a 2025 projection tied to overseas/e-commerce sales, not domestic retail growth. The strongest figure (MFDS) is on a PRODUCTION basis and is not comparable to retail sizes; the two retail estimates are LOW-confidence aggregator numbers about 2.3x apart, so absolute domestic scale remains uncertain.

passages.title: Analyst read — sun care (India)
passages.text: India sun care sizes at roughly US$0.58bn (IMARC, 2025) to US$0.89bn (TechSci, 2024) on a RETAIL basis, both LOW confidence — and these are effectively sunscreen-only sizings, which the segment-level figure already on file was built from. Sub-segment sun_protection now carries its own explicit sizings from the same houses, plus a MEDIUM-confidence K-beauty shelf-price point (Beauty of Joseon, Rs1570 MRP, [CORRIDOR]-tagged). Forecast CAGRs cluster 6.0-6.8% (IMARC, TechSci; LOW). The eye-catching +170% (2026) and +85% (2023) growth figures are quick-commerce channel and Nykaa-platform reads respectively (LOW/MEDIUM), not whole-segment growth — the category is surging on q-commerce off a small base, which is not the same as the segment growing that fast. Every size figure is a LOW aggregator estimate with a wide (~1.5x) spread and a sunscreen-only definition; the high growth numbers are channel-specific, not segment-wide, and must not be read as the market's overall rate.

passages.title: Analyst read — sun care (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both geographies now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn figures, so a directional size comparison is possible: India's sunscreen market (~US$0.58-0.89bn) is broadly comparable to, and probably somewhat larger than, Korea's retail sunscreen (~US$0.33-0.75bn) — but every figure on both sides is LOW confidence with a ~2x internal spread, so this is directional only, not a firm ranking. Korea's most reliable datapoint is production (KRW 0.47tn, MEDIUM), a different basis that cannot be set against India's retail figures. On the corridor, sun care is baseline whitespace #2: Nykaa sunscreen grew +85% YoY and Korean-sunscreen searches +148%, evidencing real K-beauty sunscreen pull into India even though no corridor-specific market size exists yet.

passages.title: Analyst read — total bpc (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's whole BPC market is anchored on a HIGH-confidence Euromonitor RETAIL figure of $13.0bn (2024), alongside a separately HIGH-confidence export figure of $11.43bn EXPORT_FOB (2025, MFDS/Korea Customs) - these sit on different value bases (domestic sell-through vs FOB shipments abroad) and are not additive. Per-capita spend of ~$250 (2024) is labelled an ESTIMATE derived in the baseline report, not a directly sourced figure. Two lower-confidence retail readings from Mordor Intelligence ($13.66bn, 2025) and Expert Market Research ($18.39bn, 2025) use a broader 'cosmetics' definition and are flagged value_basis_uncertain, so they sit alongside rather than override the Euromonitor anchor. Observed domestic retail growth was a modest 1.8% YoY in constant-value terms (2024, HIGH confidence, Euromonitor), while export growth ran far hotter at +12.3% YoY (2025) and +20.3% YoY (2024), both HIGH confidence. A LOW-confidence Mordor Intelligence figure forecasts 6.61% CAGR for 2025-2030 - a forecast, not an observed rate, and tied to a broader product basket than the headline retail size. The HIGH-confidence retail total and the HIGH-confidence export total both look solid individually but measure different things and must not be combined or netted; the only forward-looking growth figure (CAGR) carries LOW confidence and a wider product definition than the headline market size.

passages.title: Analyst read — total bpc (India)
passages.text: India's whole BPC market is sized at $33.08bn (2025) on a MEDIUM-confidence Statista/China Briefing RETAIL basis that the underlying data itself flags as value_basis_uncertain; no export figure exists at the India headline level. Per-capita spend of $22.74 (2025, MEDIUM confidence) is roughly an order of magnitude below Korea's, consistent with a much larger population base spreading the same order-of-magnitude-larger market size. Observed growth is quoted at 10.0% YoY (2024) from a LOW-confidence baseline consensus that itself notes a spread across research houses (most cluster 10-11%, some conservative ones 5-6%). The cagr_forecast of 3.48% (2025-2030, MEDIUM confidence, Statista) is a forecast only, and is notably more conservative than both the observed 10% figure and the ~10% consensus the source itself references - implying an expected deceleration versus recent history. The headline market-size figure is MEDIUM confidence and explicitly flagged value-basis-uncertain (a Statista 'consumer market revenue' read, not a confirmed RETAIL sell-through number), and there is no export or independent per-capita cross-check at the headline level.

passages.title: Analyst read — total bpc (Korea vs India)
passages.text: Both headline market-size figures carry a value_usd_bn on a RETAIL basis, so a direct size comparison is possible: India's whole BPC market ($33.08bn, MEDIUM confidence, 2025) is roughly two and a half times the size of Korea's ($13.0bn, HIGH confidence, 2024), though the reference years differ by one and the confidence levels differ. Korea additionally carries a HIGH-confidence $11.43bn EXPORT_FOB total with no India counterpart in the headline data, so exports cannot enter this comparison. Both geographies show the same reconciliation tension: neither's top-down retail figure can be checked against its bottom-up sum, because the bottom-up bases differ in currency/unit and use NET_REALISATION rather than RETAIL, and in both cases that bottom-up sum is inflated by non-pure-play conglomerates reporting revenue well beyond BPC (LG H&H in Korea; Hindustan Unilever and Godrej Consumer Products in India) - both reconciliations are marked not publishable, with gap_pct left uncomputed rather than estimated. The Korea-India corridor does not appear in either headline block, but the raw data shows Korea's exports to India are a small, fast-growing slice (~$50m in H1 2025, +44.7% YoY) and several LOW/MEDIUM-confidence India-side estimates size the K-beauty-in-India [CORRIDOR] subset at roughly $0.3-0.4bn (2024) - and now, per a second MEDIUM-confidence source (TheBK/Beauty Kyungjae, 2024-dated claim), forecast to reach roughly $1.5-1.6bn by 2030 - with high forecast CAGRs (19-26%, sources vary) - a fast-growing niche within, not representative of, either whole market.

passages.title: Corridor vector — read
passages.text: The Korea to India corridor is an import-and-curate entry route, not a build route: even AmorePacific is scaling India through platforms and imports with no India plant announced. The trade base is small but fast — baseline ~US$50m (H1 2025), +44.7% YoY — and HS 3304 imports from Korea were US$140m in 2024 (Comtrade, HIGH). Demand is proven at the platform layer (K-beauty GMV on Nykaa +60% YoY Jul-Sep 2025) and the K-beauty India market is put at ~INR 3,139cr (2025) with a ~26% CAGR to 2035 (single aggregator). A 2026 launch wave (Medicube, Illiyoon, TirTir, Hince, Dr. Melaxin) shows the corridor is actively widening. The entry decision therefore reduces to conduit choice plus clearing CDSCO — the numbers say demand and momentum are real, the friction is regulatory lead-time, and the whitespace is getting indie/derma K-beauty onto the Tier 2/3 rail rather than adding another conglomerate brand where the majors already sit.

passages.title: Corridor vector — whitespace_read
passages.text: The sharpest gap is mid-price derma K-beauty on the Tier 2/3 q-commerce rail (baseline whitespace #5, highest corridor conviction). The Blinkit snapshot makes it concrete: conglomerate-owned K-brands (AmorePacific, LG H&H) have mature India supply chains and are deeply stocked, while the indie/derma brands actually driving the K-beauty story (COSRX, Anua, Some By Mi) are out-of-stock, coming-soon or absent. The opportunity is not adding another conglomerate SKU where the majors already sit; it is getting masstige-price indie derma into dark-store distribution. Dedicated sunscreens (whitespace #2) and men's K-beauty (whitespace #4) are the adjacent gaps.

passages.title: Corridor vector — friction_read
passages.text: The binding friction is CDSCO import registration: a Form COS-1 application resolving to a COS-2 Registration Certificate via the SUGAM portal, required as pre-clearance before any consignment, plus manufacturing-site registration and BIS IS 4707 ingredient standards (Part 2 revised Aug 2025). Paper filings are no longer accepted as of 2026. This is a lead-time and working-capital cost rather than a hard barrier, but it must be cleared before the first shipment — cost and timeline are not yet quantified in the data and remain a research-needed item.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Nykaa
passages.text: Primary conduit and the deepest Korean assortment in India: a 10-year AmorePacific partnership (2016-2026) plus a widening exclusives book (Illiyoon, Aestura, RYO, Mise En Scene) and now non-AmorePacific indie brands (TirTir, Medicube). It is the only conduit with a published corridor demand signal — K-beauty GMV +60% YoY Jul-Sep 2025 — and is the exclusive launch pad for the K-derma wave. First choice for a premium/derma entrant.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Tira
passages.text: Reliance Retail's omnichannel platform running an aggressive 2026 K-beauty sprint built on exclusives (Hince Jan-2026, Dr. Melaxin exclusive Jul-2026, Medicube Feb-2026, Mixsoon since 2024). Its exclusive-launch model makes it the strongest alternative to Nykaa for a brand wanting a differentiated shelf and Reliance's store + online reach, though no corridor GMV figure is published for it.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — q-commerce
passages.text: Blinkit/Zepto/Instamart are the Tier 2/3 access rail and the corridor's clearest whitespace, but the assortment is uneven: a single Blinkit snapshot (2026-07-23, 63 K-brand SKUs) shows conglomerate brands stocked deep (The Face Shop 21 SKUs, Laneige 16) while the viral indie/derma brands driving the narrative (COSRX, Anua, Some By Mi) are out-of-stock, 'coming soon' or absent. High strategic value, thin current execution for indie derma.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Flipkart
passages.text: Launched an international K-beauty portfolio (2025) weighted to indie brands (Beauty of Joseon, rom&nd, TirTir, Thank You Farmer). Broad indie reach at mass scale, but the evidence is a launch note only — no assortment depth, exclusives or demand signal recorded.

passages.title: Corridor conduit ranking — Amazon
passages.text: Carries a spread of indie K-brands (Anua, Some By Mi, Isntree, Dr.Jart+, Etude, The Face Shop). Useful for reach and long-tail discovery, but only a brand list is recorded — no exclusives, assortment depth or corridor demand data to rank it higher.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — skinification (India)
passages.text: The active-ingredient logic of skincare is migrating into hair care: demand is moving from mass shampoo toward serums and scalp tonics carrying named actives, and the finding explicitly flags specialist D2C outpacing legacy FMCG. It reframes hair care as a treatment category rather than a cleansing one, which favours ingredient-led entrants over shelf-space incumbents. Note the underlying India hair-care sizing is LOW-confidence and internally conflicting (Mordor 4.73% vs IMARC 10.58% CAGR), so the direction is well-evidenced but the magnitude is not.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — glass-skin/K-beauty pull (India)
passages.text: K-drama/K-pop-led aspiration is converting into category-specific search and transaction demand, concentrated in derma-adjacent skincare and sunscreen where the 'glass skin' aesthetic is most legible. This is the corridor's demand engine: it is documented as a channel signal (Nykaa GMV, platform search spikes) rather than an independent market size, and the K-beauty India totals rest on a single aggregator, so treat it as a strong directional pull with soft absolute sizing.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — access-led q-commerce shift (India)
passages.text: Quick commerce has become the default access rail into Tier 2/3, turning beauty from an aspiration-led into an availability-led purchase. BPC is growing far faster on q-commerce than overall, which reshapes route-to-market: dark-store availability, not brand awareness, is becoming the binding constraint on volume. The GMV split is single-sourced and the sunscreen surge is a LOW-confidence projection, but the structural shift is corroborated across multiple Redseer reads.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — premiumization (India)
passages.text: Willingness to pay is rising within categories, not just across them: premium and masstige tiers are the fastest-growing slices even inside value-conscious channels like q-commerce, and imports cluster at the premium/K-beauty end. The masstige-derma tier is the clearest quantified expression of this. The signal is qualitative-plus-LOW-confidence sizing, so it supports a premium-tier entry thesis without a defensible premium market-size number.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — men's grooming rise (India)
passages.text: Men's grooming is the segment with the firmest India demand base in the set — a HIGH-confidence Euromonitor size growing ~9% — with the skincare sub-slice growing faster still. It is simultaneously flagged as corridor whitespace because men's skincare is underserved relative to toiletries. The size and growth are well-evidenced; the sub-slice CAGR and the whitespace read are softer, so the opportunity framing is stronger than any precise men's-skincare number.

passages.title: Demand Drivers — premiumization (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's mature domestic skincare market (~+1% YoY) is growing almost entirely through premium active-ingredient derma: dermocosmetics is up ~13% on next-generation actives (PDRN, exosomes, peptides). Value growth is coming from ingredient escalation inside a flat volume base, which is what feeds the export and corridor story. This is the best-evidenced driver in the set (both points Euromonitor HIGH), but it describes the source market, not an India demand pull.

passages.title: Entry mode — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: partner. A domestic share play in Korean skincare is not attractive and the mode call should be read that way. The scorecard scores size 5 (KRW 7.653tn retail, HIGH) but growth 2 — domestic retail is +1.0% YoY (Euromonitor, HIGH) — and porter_skincare rates rivalry HIGH (STRONG) with new-entrant threat HIGH: a near-flat market, a listed duopoly at the top, and near-zero barriers underneath compress economics for anyone buying share. What Korea is genuinely good for is origination, and that is what the mode reflects: partner with the ODM/OEM base (Cosmax, Kolmar Korea, Cosmecca — all named, all competing, supplier power LOW) to formulate and fill, and partner into the concentrated shelf (Olive Young holds >85% of the H&B store market at 1,380+ stores, and rtm_KR reads it as a near-gatekeeper). That is an asset-light presence that produces corridor-ready product, not a domestic share contest. Alternatives: build was rejected: owning production in the world's densest contract-manufacturing market duplicates capacity that is already commoditised, into +1% domestic demand. acquire has no grounding — the repo records no KR skincare M&A transaction to benchmark a multiple against (the only exit multiple on file, HUL/Minimalist at 8.5x, is Indian). import_corridor is directionally wrong: the corridor in this dataset runs KR->IN, and Korea is its source, so corridor_tailwind is literally null on every KR row.

passages.title: Entry mode — skincare (India)
passages.text: Mode: partner. India skincare is the largest documented prize in the dataset (US$9.06bn RETAIL, LOW) with the richest channel access (score 4, STRONG) and a strong corridor pull (score 4, STRONG: HS 3304 imports from Korea US$0.14bn in 2024, K-brands across Nykaa and Blinkit). But an unaided import play buys the most contested shelf at the highest take. porter_skincare rates IN rivalry HIGH (STRONG) and buyer power HIGH: Nykaa charges 22-26% on skincare plus GST, q-commerce runs ~38% all-in on MRP, and the Blinkit snapshot shows the conglomerate K-brands already deeply stocked (The Face Shop 21 SKUs, Laneige 16, Innisfree 9) — the general K-skincare slot is taken. The defensible mode is therefore partnering into a conduit rather than arriving alone: the evidenced entry pattern is the platform relationship itself (Nykaa's 10-year AmorePacific tie-up; Tira's 2026 exclusive-launch sprint), which buys placement and marketing weight the entrant cannot self-fund against a 22-28% take. Alternatives: import_corridor unaided is the obvious alternative and remains viable on the demand evidence, but it lands into HIGH rivalry and HIGH buyer power with no shelf guarantee and a 3-9 month CDSCO wait ahead of first revenue (regulatory.json) — the reason it is second, not first. build via India contract manufacturing (the Limese/Pilgrim Korean-ingredient template, MOQs ~500 units) escapes CDSCO entirely and is credible at mass Rs500-700 price points, but forfeits Korean-origin authenticity, which is the entrant's only differentiator here. acquire is unsupported: the sole India beauty exit benchmark on file is HUL/Minimalist at ~8.5x revenue, which prices consolidation richly and is a dermocosmetics, not general-skincare, datapoint.

passages.title: Entry mode — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not recommendable on current evidence. The scorecard scores only 2 of 6 criteria (size 3, growth 3, both on a production/aggregator basis: MFDS sunscreen production KRW 0.4703tn MEDIUM against retail estimates 2.3x apart), with competitive openness, channel access and regulatory friction all INSUFFICIENT. porter_sun_care reads KR sun care as a production and export strength rather than a domestic-share opportunity — which is a useful read for sourcing, but not enough to name an entry mode into the Korean market itself. Alternatives: No mode is named because the choice between building, partnering with the sunscreen-capable ODM base (Kolmar Korea is directly named as the OTC-sunscreen contract manufacturer behind US exports) and acquiring cannot be discriminated without any share, channel or regulatory-cost evidence. Naming one would be a hedged guess.

passages.title: Entry mode — sun care (India)
passages.text: Mode: import_corridor. The cleanest corridor import case after dermocosmetics, and it scores 3.5 on all 6 criteria. Demand pull is specific and evidenced rather than inferred: 'Korean sunscreen' searches +148% and 'glass skin' +61% in a quarter, top Korean brands +50% on Nykaa, Nykaa platform sunscreen sales +85% YoY, and Beauty of Joseon's Relief Sunscreen (Rs1,570 MRP) a category bestseller — consumers are already asking for Korean-origin SPF by name, which is exactly the demand an import play monetises and a domestic build cannot claim. The category is underpenetrated (baseline whitespace #2) and rising fastest on the access rail (q-commerce sunscreen projected +170% in 2026), so the shelf is expanding rather than defended. Regulatory friction is now quantified and manageable: a narrow SPF hero range from a single Korean ODM plant registers for roughly USD 1,000-2,000 per category plus USD 50/variant and USD 500/site, on a 3-9 month clock, against a COS-2 valid 5 years. Alternatives: build (domestic sunscreen manufacture) is genuinely feasible — India has a large sunscreen base and supplier power is LOW — and it sidesteps CDSCO, but it discards the Korean-origin signal the search and Nykaa data show is doing the selling. partner with a conduit is the closest second and can be layered on top: the q-commerce whitespace is a distribution problem, not a registration problem. acquire is unsupported — no India sun-care acquisition is recorded in the repo.

passages.title: Entry mode — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: partner. Korea's highest scorecard composite (3.7) but on only 3 of 6 criteria, and the strength is export-shaped: size is triangulated across three bases (retail US$2.86bn LOW, production KRW 2.84tn MEDIUM, export US$1.51bn HIGH) and growth is strongest on exactly the export and production bases (+12% EXPORT_FOB HIGH, +51.4% production). As a domestic share play it is unattractive on the same logic as skincare — porter_colour rates KR rivalry HIGH and new-entrant threat HIGH, a crowded field where the ODM base lets anyone launch. The mode that the evidence does support is partner: Korea's colour ODM/OEM ecosystem (supplier power LOW) plus the Olive Young shelf is a brand-origination and export platform, and the indie route the corridor already carries (rom&nd, Hince, Etude reaching India) is the proof that this is how value leaves Korea. Alternatives: build is hard to justify when three listed ODM houses compete for the work. acquire cannot be grounded — no KR colour transaction or valuation is on file. A domestic share contest against LG H&H/AmorePacific plus the indie long tail is rejected outright: rivalry HIGH with easy entry is the structural definition of compressed returns.

passages.title: Entry mode — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Mode: partner. Scored on all 6 criteria (3.2) with channel access STRONG but the two structural drags both point away from arriving alone: the mass tier holds ~79.55% of the market (Mordor), and colour carries the highest platform commission band of any category (Nykaa 24-28%) with buyer power rated HIGH in porter_colour. Meanwhile the corridor evidence shows precisely how Korean colour has actually entered India — as platform exclusives: Hince launched exclusive on Tira in Jan-2026, rom&nd via Flipkart's international K-beauty portfolio, Etude on Amazon. That is a partner motion, not an independent import build, and Amazon's cut of make-up referral fees to 3.5% (Sep-2025) shows platforms actively bidding for this category's supply. Partnering into a conduit exclusive buys the placement and launch weight that a 24-28% take otherwise consumes. Alternatives: import_corridor unaided is credible on demand but corridor_tailwind scores only 3 (PARTIAL) — colour is a secondary K-beauty axis behind skincare and derma — so the pull is not strong enough to carry an independent import cost base against mass-tier price expectations. build via contract manufacturing is cheap (supplier power LOW) but lands in HIGH rivalry against funded platform-native D2C (SUGAR, Plum) and MNC incumbents. acquire has no India colour transaction on file to price.

passages.title: Entry mode — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable. The scorecard scores zero of six criteria: KR fragrances carries only an export figure (US$0.06bn EXPORT_FOB, +46.2% off a tiny base) with no domestic size, growth, shares, channel or regulatory data. porter_fragrances calls the KR side a data-void segment and declines to rate any of the five forces. No entry mode can be named without inventing the market structure. Alternatives: None assessable. Even the supplier-side logic that carries other KR segments does not transfer — porter notes Korea's general cosmetics ODM base does not extend cleanly to fine-fragrance perfumery, so the usual 'partner with the ODM base' fallback is itself unevidenced here.

passages.title: Entry mode — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Mode: build. Scored on all 6 criteria but the lowest composite in the dataset (2.5), and the mode has to be read alongside a blunt finding: there is effectively no KR->IN fragrance corridor. HS 3303 imports from Korea were US$0.000135bn in 2024 and no Korean fragrance brand entry is recorded — corridor_tailwind scores 1 on evidenced near-absence, so a Korean-origin entrant has no advantage in this segment at all. What the evidence does support, for an entrant generally, is a domestic build: mass perfume and deodorant are filled domestically through contract manufacturing (supplier power LOW at mass, new-entrant threat HIGH), D2C fragrance is actively funded, and the incumbent concentration is a single KKR-controlled leader (Vini/Fogg, INR 1,200cr FY25) rather than a wall of MNCs. The premium tier is the part to avoid on an import basis: porter records it as import-reliant on UAE, France and Germany for oils and finished goods — supply routes that run through the Gulf, not Korea. Alternatives: import_corridor is rejected on direct evidence, not judgement — the KR->IN fragrance trade flow is effectively zero. partner with a conduit is weak because fragrance-specific channel depth is missing (only a Nykaa 22-25% commission datapoint exists; GT/MT and gifting weight are unrecorded), so there is no conduit case to partner into. acquire is unsupported — the only ownership datapoint is KKR's 54% of Vini, a control position at a scale that is not an entry vehicle.

passages.title: Entry mode — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not recommendable on 2 of 6 criteria. Size rests on a single LOW aggregator figure (US$1.8bn, IMARC 2025, with other aggregators clustering ~US$1.30bn) and growth on a LOW CAGR forecast alone (3.23%) with no observed growth_yoy; openness, channel and regulatory are all INSUFFICIENT. porter_hair_care rates the KR read THIN overall and frames Korea as a source of formulation and corridor SKUs rather than a domestic-share opportunity — a sourcing observation, not an entry recommendation. Alternatives: The ODM-partner logic that carries KR skincare and colour is plausible here too (Cosmax/Kolmar/Cosmecca supply hair formulation as readily as skincare, supplier power LOW), but with no shares, no channel data and a modest LOW-confidence market, naming partner would be extrapolation from adjacent segments rather than a grounded call.

passages.title: Entry mode — hair care (India)
passages.text: Mode: partner. Scored on all 6 criteria but weakly (2.7), and it is the least attractive of the fully-scored India rows. The market is large (US$4.1-4.30bn, LOW) but incumbent-owned in the mass base (shampoo 45%, conditioners 42.71% product-type concentration; HUL/Godrej-era majors), growth is genuinely unresolved (Mordor 4.73% vs IMARC 10.58%, flagged do-not-reconcile), and the corridor is thin — HS 3305 imports from Korea were only US$0.0033bn in 2024 despite AmorePacific putting Mise En Scene and RYO on Nykaa in 2025. porter_hair_care also records active substitution away from topicals toward ingestibles in the hair-growth space. Given all that, the only route with live evidence behind it is the one AmorePacific itself used: partner into the Nykaa conduit for the premium/actives lane, rather than building a mass presence against incumbents or importing at scale into a US$3.3m trade flow. Alternatives: build into the skinification/scalp-actives edge via contract manufacturing is the strategic alternative and matches where growth is — but porter records that lane as already crowded with well-funded D2C (Honasa, Innovist's Bare Anatomy), so it trades an incumbent fight for a funded-challenger fight. import_corridor is not supported by the trade evidence (corridor_tailwind 2, THIN). acquire has no India hair-care transaction on file.

passages.title: Entry mode — bath shower (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable — and uniquely so: bath_shower is the one taxonomy segment with no entry_scorecard row at all, so there is not even a partial composite to reason from. gaps.json records the KR side as carrying export_value only, with market_size, growth_yoy and cagr_forecast all missing, and no porter artifact exists for the segment. Alternatives: None. With no size, no structure and no scorecard row, every mode would be pure assertion.

passages.title: Entry mode — bath shower (India)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable. gaps.json records 'no data' for IN bath_shower on market_size, growth_yoy and cagr_forecast alike, there is no entry_scorecard row, no porter artifact, and no [CORRIDOR] datapoint linking Korean bath and shower products to India. This is a coverage hole rather than a negative finding — soaps and body washes are a large part of Indian BPC by volume, and the repo simply has not researched them. Alternatives: None.
