Naming a mode for a segment with zero DataPoints would be exactly the hedged guess the grounding rules forbid.

passages.title: Entry mode — deodorants (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable. The scorecard scores zero of six criteria and gaps.json records 'no data' for KR deodorants on every metric — no size, no growth, no shares, no channel, no regulatory evidence. There is no porter artifact for the segment either. Alternatives: None assessable on zero DataPoints.

passages.title: Entry mode — deodorants (India)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable, despite deodorants plainly being a real Indian market: the only figure that touches it is the US$2.6bn IN fragrances number, which explicitly bundles perfume and deodorant and is therefore not a deo-specific measure. The scorecard scores zero of six criteria. Vini/Fogg's INR 1,200cr FY25 revenue sits in the fragrances row and cannot be re-used as a deodorants sizing without deriving an implied statistic across DataPoints. Alternatives: None named. The temptation is to inherit the fragrances read (build, domestic contract manufacturing) since the categories overlap commercially — but that would be an inference across a definitional boundary the repo has explicitly flagged, so it is left unnamed.

passages.title: Entry mode — oral care (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable. The scorecard scores zero of six criteria: KR oral care carries only an HS 3306 export figure (US$0.08bn EXPORT_FOB, 2024) with no domestic size, growth, shares, channel or regulatory data, and gaps.json confirms market_size and growth are missing. Alternatives: None assessable — an export value alone cannot discriminate between entry modes into a domestic market.

passages.title: Entry mode — oral care (India)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not recommendable: only 1 of 6 criteria is scorable, and that one criterion is a negative — corridor_tailwind scores 1 because HS 3306 imports from Korea were US$0.000485bn in 2024 with no Korean oral-care brand entry recorded. There is no size, growth, share or channel evidence, and the regulatory pathway is itself unresolved because oral care straddles cosmetic and drug classification in India and the repo's regulatory research covers cosmetics only. The one thing the data does say is that the corridor gives a Korean entrant nothing here. Alternatives: None named. A build or partner read would require knowing the incumbent structure, and the major Indian toothpaste incumbents are not in the dataset at all.

passages.title: Entry mode — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not recommendable on 2 of 6 criteria. Size is reasonably evidenced (KRW 1.16tn, ~US$0.78bn 2025, Euromonitor MEDIUM) but growth is disputed between an FMI forecast of 11.04% and an Euromonitor-implied ~2.1% off the 2022-2025 series, with no observed growth_yoy; openness, channel and regulatory are all INSUFFICIENT. porter_mens_grooming rates the KR read THIN overall and positions Korea as a source of proven men's-skincare formulation rather than a share opportunity. Alternatives: The ODM-partner logic applies in principle (supplier power LOW, asset-light launches straightforward) but with a growth rate that is unresolved by a factor of five and no channel or share data, a mode call would rest on adjacent-segment inference rather than this segment's evidence.

passages.title: Entry mode — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Mode: build. The best-evidenced India segment on the two criteria that matter most — size INR 186.3bn (~US$1.94bn) 2025 at HIGH confidence and observed growth +9% YoY at HIGH confidence, both Euromonitor, corroborated by IBEF and IMARC. Channel access is STRONG and quantified (e-commerce 30-35% of urban men's grooming; online 27.2% share and the fastest-growing tier). Crucially, the corridor cannot carry this one: corridor_tailwind scores 2 (THIN) because men's K-beauty is a flagged whitespace (#4) with no live Korean men's product entry recorded — a latent opportunity, not traction. So the mode that the evidence supports is build: launch a dedicated men's skincare/beard line through India's contract-manufacturing base (supplier power LOW, MOQs ~500 units) into the explicitly underserved men's-skincare lane, distributed on the online tier where the growth is. This is the one India row where building is better-grounded than partnering or importing, because the demand evidence is domestic and HIGH-confidence while the corridor evidence is speculative. Alternatives: import_corridor is the tempting read given whitespace #4, but it is unsupported — no men's-specific Korean product entry exists in the data, so importing would be a bet on an unactivated whitespace rather than an observed pull. partner with a conduit is a reasonable overlay for distribution but does not address the actual gap, which is product for an underserved lane rather than shelf access (online access is already documented as strong). acquire has no India men's-grooming transaction on file to price.

passages.title: Entry mode — baby child (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable. The scorecard scores zero of six criteria and gaps.json records 'no data' for KR baby/child on every metric. No porter artifact, no company evidence, no corridor linkage. Alternatives: None assessable on zero DataPoints.

passages.title: Entry mode — baby child (India)
passages.text: Mode: research needed. Not evaluable. The scorecard scores zero of six criteria, gaps.json records 'no data' throughout, and no KR->IN baby/child trade or brand-entry DataPoint exists. Worth flagging that this is a coverage gap in a segment with obvious commercial weight in India, not a judgement that the segment is unattractive. Alternatives: None. Every mode would be assertion.

passages.title: Entry mode — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Mode: partner. Scored on 3 of 6 criteria (composite 3.3) and carrying the firmest growth signal in the Korean dataset: +13% YoY 2024 at HIGH confidence (Euromonitor), driven by an actives race (PDRN, exosomes, peptides). Unlike KR skincare, this is not a flat market — but it is still not a domestic share play an outsider wins by building, because porter_dermocosmetics rates rivalry HIGH with the majors holding derma brands (AmorePacific's Aestura and Illiyoon) atop a broad indie and ODM base. The route the evidence supports is partner: the ODM base extends into actives-heavy derma formulation (supplier power LOW), and MFDS approval is cheap and fast where a formulation reuses pre-approved functional actives (~7 days, ~KRW 189,000) — so partnering for formulation and shelf gives access to the actives frontier without owning either. The strategic case is compounded by the corridor: a KR derma position is the supply side of India's highest-conviction whitespace. Alternatives: build is weakened by the same ODM depth that makes partnering cheap, and by the one real supplier caveat porter flags — frontier actives are the exception to LOW supplier power. acquire is unsupported: no KR derma transaction or multiple is recorded (APR/Medicube appears in the data as an India entrant, not as an acquisition target with a price). A domestic share contest is rejected on rivalry HIGH plus a definitionally unresolved market size (Korean sources ~4x apart, KRW 1.2tn to KRW 4.5tn).

passages.title: Entry mode — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: Mode: import_corridor. The layer's headline entry case and the highest-conviction import call in the dataset. It scores 3.5 on all 6 criteria with the strongest corridor tailwind in the taxonomy (5, STRONG): baseline whitespace #1 is mid-price derma K-beauty in Tier 2/3, Nykaa K-beauty GMV is +60% YoY (Q3 2025, MEDIUM), and a 2026 launch wave is already landing (Medicube on Nykaa and Tira, Illiyoon Nykaa-exclusive, Aestura, Dr. Melaxin exclusive to Tira). Competitive openness is 4 (STRONG) with a proven exit benchmark — Minimalist at INR 347cr FY24 revenue acquired by HUL at INR 2,955cr, ~8.5x — showing the category creates real value. The import route is the right one specifically because the whitespace is Korean-origin derma: corridor_vector reads the corridor as an import-and-curate route, noting even AmorePacific is scaling India through platforms and imports with no India plant announced. The single real cost is CDSCO, and regulatory.json now sizes it: roughly USD 1,000-2,000 per category plus USD 50/variant and USD 500/site, 3-9 months to COS-2, valid 5 years — a lead-time and working-capital cost, not a barrier, and one that argues for a tight hero-SKU range from a single ODM plant. The gap to attack is dark-store distribution, where the Blinkit snapshot shows conglomerate brands deep-stocked while indie derma (COSRX out-of-stock, Anua 'coming soon', Some By Mi absent) is missing. Alternatives: partner with a conduit is the necessary complement rather than a rival — the import decision reduces to conduit choice, with Nykaa ranked first (deepest Korean assortment, the only conduit with a published corridor demand signal) and Tira second on its exclusive-launch model. build via India contract manufacturing avoids CDSCO entirely and is the Limese/Pilgrim template, but a made-in-India derma line surrenders the Korean-origin claim that is the whole basis of the +60% GMV pull, and drops into the most contested lane in Indian beauty (rivalry HIGH, STRONG). acquire is priced against a single benchmark (8.5x revenue) that reflects a strategic FMCG buyer, and there is no evidence of available India derma assets at entry scale.

Note that two of the listed sub-segments — ayurvedic/herbal and K-beauty derivatives — are commercially live in India on the evidence of adjacent segments, so this is a taxonomy and coverage problem rather than an absence of market. passages.title: Entry scorecard — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Composite 3.3 based on 3 of 6 criteria. partial — based on 3 of 6 criteria. The prize is both large and firmly evidenced (the two bases must not be summed, but each is well-sourced).; growth_evidence: 2/5 — Domestic retail is essentially flat: +1.0% YoY 2025 (Euromonitor, HIGH) — a mature, saturated home market, hence low attractiveness for a domestic-entry play. The +11.6% export growth is HIGH but sits on EXPORT_FOB, not domestic sell-through, so it does not lift the home-market growth read.; competitive_openness: 3/5 — Top of market is a listed duopoly (LG H&H, AmorePacific) but the deep ODM/OEM base (Cosmax, Kolmar Korea, named as excluded value-chain levels) lowers barriers for indie skincare brands — the engine behind K-beauty's long tail. passages.title: Entry scorecard — skincare (India)
passages.text: Composite 3.3 based on 6 of 6 criteria. full — all 6 criteria scored. Large, channel-rich, corridor-backed market; held back by LOW-confidence sizing and absent segment growth data. market_size_evidence: 3/5 — Large market — US$9.06bn retail 2025 (IMARC) — with multiple corroborating sub-segment sizings (face wash US$1.23bn, facial masks, serum), but every figure is LOW-confidence aggregator with unstated organised/unorganised coverage. Big prize, thin evidence quality.; growth_evidence: 2/5 — No segment-level growth_yoy exists (gaps.json flags it missing); the only forward number is a serum-sub-segment CAGR of 5.99% (LOW, IMARC). Growth direction for the segment as a whole cannot be read from current data.; competitive_openness: 4/5 — Open and being actively disrupted: mass tier (<Rs200) holds ~40% (Pond's/Nivea/Himalaya/Lakme/Garnier) but D2C challengers are winning share (Minimalist revenue Rs184cr->Rs347cr FY23->FY24) and Korean brands are entering at masstige — a fragmenting, contestable field despite conglomerate weight at total-BPC level (HUL 78.6% of listed owners).; channel_access: 4/5 — Richest channel access in the dataset: multiple documented conduits (Nykaa, Tira, Flipkart, Amazon) plus the q-commerce rail carrying entry-price K-beauty (Face Shop, Innisfree, Laneige on Blinkit). Trade cost is quantified (Nykaa skincare commission 22-26%), so the route to shelf is well-mapped — margin is the price of easy access.; regulatory_friction: 3/5 — CDSCO import registration (Form COS-1 -> COS-2 via SUGAM, site registration, BIS IS 4707, no paper filings) is real, documented friction for imports — but skincare is ~91% domestically supplied (import dependence 9.3%, ESTIMATE), so a local-manufacture route largely sidesteps it. Net friction is moderate.; corridor_tailwind: 4/5 — Strong, well-documented KR->IN pull: a large set of [CORRIDOR]-tagged K-beauty SKUs live on Nykaa/Blinkit (COSRX, Laneige, Innisfree, Anua, Beauty of Joseon, Face Shop), HS 3304 imports from Korea of US$0.14bn (2024), and glass-skin demand. Skincare is the corridor's core axis, second only to derma in conviction.
