passages.text: India's contract-manufacturing findings are scoped to beauty/skincare D2C and say nothing about baby-care fill, which carries stricter safety and testing obligations. No baby-care supply DataPoint exists, so the adjacency is noted but not rated. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN baby-care manufacturing structure, safety-testing and import dependence — absent.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — baby child (India)
passages.text: No size, no barrier evidence, and no launch or funding record scoped to India baby & child. The ~US$757m of India D2C beauty/wellness funding on file is not attributed to any baby-care brand, so it cannot carry an entry read for this segment. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN baby_child entry evidence (new brands, funding, CDSCO/BIS applicability to baby products) — absent.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — baby child (India)
passages.text: No substitution evidence. For India this would also require the organised-versus-unorganised split — traditional and home-prepared baby-care practice is precisely the substitute in question — and that split is unrecorded. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN baby_child substitution and unorganised-share evidence — absent.

passages.title: Porter overall — baby child (India)
passages.text: A confirmed void on both sides of the corridor: neither geography has a single DataPoint, so no KR-versus-IN comparison and no corridor read is possible. Baby & child is also absent from corridor.yaml — no K-brand carried into India is tagged to it, and it is not among the three ranked whitespace opportunities (mid-price derma in Tier 2/3, dedicated sunscreens, men's K-beauty). On current evidence this segment is outside the corridor's demonstrated path, though that reflects what has been researched, not a finding that the opportunity is absent. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Run the gaps.json IN/baby_child rows (market_size, growth_yoy, cagr_forecast) before any force is rated.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — bath shower (South Korea)
passages.text: There is no Korean domestic market size, growth rate or brand share for bath & shower in this repo — the single figure on file is an export value. LG H&H is the only company in the register tagged to the segment, and a one-name field with no shares cannot support an intensity rating. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR bath_shower domestic market size, growth and brand shares — gaps.json rows KR/bath_shower market_size + growth_yoy + cagr_forecast (suggested: euromonitor_passport, statista, korea_mfds, tavily).

passages.title: Porter buyer power — bath shower (South Korea)
passages.text: No KR bath-and-shower channel or margin evidence exists. Body cleansing is a mass/grocery format in most markets, so the CJ Olive Young and duty-free structure the repo documents for cosmetics cannot be assumed to govern it, and duty-free in particular is a distinct channel that must not be folded into a domestic read. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR bath_shower channel split and retail margins — no channel DataPoint exists for this segment (euromonitor_passport, korea_mfds).

passages.title: Porter supplier power — bath shower (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Korea shipped US$0.59bn FOB of 'body cleansing products' in 2025 (HIGH, MFDS via Yonhap/Korea Herald) — the third-largest of the four segment export values on file, behind skincare (US$8.54bn) and colour cosmetics (US$1.51bn) and far ahead of fragrances (US$0.06bn), all same year and same EXPORT_FOB basis. An export flow of that size evidences scaled, export-qualified production capacity standing behind the category rather than a boutique make. Against that, Korea's brand owners have three listed contract manufacturers to choose from (Cosmax, Kolmar Korea, Cosmecca Korea) plus in-house capacity at LG H&H, so no single maker holds pricing leverage over a brand owner. This is an inference from the export flow and the ODM roster — there is no bath-specific supplier, cost or margin DataPoint — hence THIN. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — bath shower (South Korea)
passages.text: The ODM depth that suppresses supplier power would ordinarily also lower the capital barrier to launching a body-wash brand, but the repo holds no bath-specific regulatory pathway, no launch record, and no funding evidence for this segment — and with no domestic market size there is no measurable prize to enter. Rating this on the skincare analogy alone would be a hedged guess. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR bath_shower domestic market size plus MFDS pathway/launch evidence before entry barriers can be rated.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — bath shower (South Korea)
passages.text: No evidence of substitution between body cleansing and adjacent formats (bar soap, body-care skincare, in-shower treatments) exists for Korea in the repo. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR bath_shower substitution evidence (soap vs body wash vs body-care skinification) — absent (euromonitor_passport, tavily).

passages.title: Porter overall — bath shower (South Korea)
passages.text: Export-visible, domestically unmeasured. The US$0.59bn 2025 export flow is a genuine, HIGH-confidence signal that Korea has scaled body-cleansing manufacturing and international demand for it — enough to rate supplier power LOW and to make the category interesting as a sourcing base. It says nothing about the Korean home market, which has no size, growth or share data at all, so no attractiveness call for a domestic-share entrant is defensible. Note the export figure is the customs 'body cleansing products' category and must not be read as domestic retail. Evidence strength: PARTIAL. Research needed: KR bath_shower domestic retail size and shares (gaps.json) before an attractiveness read.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — bath shower (India)
passages.text: India bath & shower has zero DataPoints — no processed file, no size, no growth, no shares, and no company in the register is tagged to the segment (HUL's tags are skincare, hair_care, colour_cosmetics, deodorants). There is nothing to rate against. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN bath_shower market size, growth and organised/unorganised split — gaps.json rows IN/bath_shower market_size + growth_yoy + cagr_forecast (suggested: euromonitor_passport, statista, tavily).

passages.title: Porter buyer power — bath shower (India)
passages.text: No India bath-and-shower channel evidence exists. The repo's India channel data is beauty-platform-shaped (Nykaa commission bands, q-commerce GMV split); body wash and soap route primarily through GT/MT, which the repo has not measured for this segment. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN bath_shower channel split (GT/MT/q-commerce) and trade margins — absent.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — bath shower (India)
passages.text: The India contract-manufacturing findings on file (third-party private-label houses at ~500-unit MOQs; Galaxy Surfactants supplying mild surfactants for cleansers) are plausibly adjacent to body cleansing, but they were gathered as a beauty/skincare D2C finding and no bath-and-shower DataPoint anchors them to this segment. Not rated on adjacency alone. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN bath_shower manufacturing structure and import dependence — no segment DataPoint exists.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — bath shower (India)
passages.text: No market size, no barrier evidence, no launch or funding record scoped to India bath & shower. Nothing to rate. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN bath_shower entry evidence (new brands, funding, CDSCO applicability to body cleansing) — absent.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — bath shower (India)
passages.text: No substitution evidence exists. In India specifically the soap-versus-body-wash question and the unorganised share would both be central to this force, and neither is recorded. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN bath_shower substitution and unorganised-share evidence (bar soap vs body wash) — absent.

passages.title: Porter overall — bath shower (India)
passages.text: A confirmed data void: not one DataPoint exists for India bath & shower on either the market or the corridor side, and the segment is not listed among corridor.yaml's K-beauty-carried categories. This is a registered gap, not a zero market — the segment should be read as unresearched, and nothing here should be treated as even a low-confidence estimate. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Run the gaps.json IN/bath_shower rows (market_size, growth_yoy, cagr_forecast) before any force is rated.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Two listed conglomerates (AmorePacific, LG H&H) both carry colour cosmetics, and a deep ODM base (Cosmax, Kolmar, Cosmecca) has enabled a long tail of indie brands (rom&nd, Etude, Hince) to proliferate and compete for the same shelf and export demand. Colour-cosmetics factory-gate output surged +51.4% YoY in 2024 (MFDS via Personal Care Insights, MEDIUM), a supply push that intensifies competition for placement. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. CJ Olive Young is the dominant health-and-beauty retail gatekeeper for Korean colour cosmetics (listed as the KR retailer conduit), giving concentrated channel leverage over brands, but no Korea-specific trade-margin or channel-share figure is in the repo to size that leverage precisely. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: No KR colour-cosmetics channel-concentration or trade-margin DataPoint exists; a retail-margin / Olive Young share figure would firm this rating.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Korea hosts three listed, competing ODM/OEM houses (Cosmax, Kolmar, Cosmecca) plus a wider contract base, so brand owners can source formulation and fill from multiple suppliers on commodity terms. A fragmented, capable supplier tier keeps input-side bargaining power low for colour-cosmetics brands. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. The same deep ODM base lets a new brand launch colour cosmetics without owning a factory, which is exactly how Korea's indie wave (rom&nd, Hince, Beauty of Joseon) reached market and then the corridor. MFDS registration exists but is not a scale barrier against the low formulation-and-fill cost of entry. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: No adjacent-segment substitution evidence for Korean colour cosmetics is present in the repo (e.g. no data on skincare-hybrids or tinted-care displacing makeup). Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Substitution read requires adjacent-segment evidence (e.g. tinted skincare / cushion-hybrid displacement) not currently in segment or insights data.

passages.title: Porter overall — colour cosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Korea's colour cosmetics is a manufacturing-and-export hub with intense rivalry and easy entry (low supplier power, deep ODM base) but concentrated retail gatekeeping. Structurally crowded on the supply side; attractive as a sourcing/export origin rather than a low-competition domestic entry. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. India colour cosmetics (US$3.46bn 2024, LOW) is mass-tier-dominated (79.55% mass share, Mordor 2025) and contested by MNC incumbents (HUL, L'Oreal India), platform-native D2C (SUGAR, Plum), and active strategic consolidation (HUL acquiring Minimalist and Plum). A crowded mass base plus M&A land-grab signals high competitive intensity. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Beauty platforms take the highest commission band of any category on colour cosmetics — Nykaa 24-28% — and concentrated q-commerce (Blinkit ~45-50%) is now a default access rail, so a small number of channel gatekeepers set the terms of shelf access and economics for entrants. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Indian brands overwhelmingly use third-party contract manufacturers / private-label houses (MOQs from ~500 units) rather than owning production, and specialty inputs come from established suppliers (Galaxy Surfactants, Fine Organics). A fragmented, agile CM base keeps supplier bargaining power low for colour brands. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Low production barriers (contract manufacturing) plus a strong D2C funding record (~US$757m into India beauty/wellness D2C over 18 months) make brand launch cheap and well-capitalised. CDSCO import registration (COS-1 to COS-2 via SUGAM) is a real barrier only for imported entrants, not domestic launches. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: No adjacent-segment substitution evidence for India colour cosmetics is present in the repo. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Substitution read requires adjacent-segment evidence (e.g. tinted skincare / BB-CC displacement of colour makeup) not in current data.

passages.title: Porter overall — colour cosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. India colour cosmetics is large and growing (forecast ~7-8% CAGR) with easy production-side entry, but rivalry is high, channel gatekeepers extract the category's top commission band, and incumbents are consolidating the best D2C assets. Attractive on size and growth, but not a low-competition or low-channel-cost entry. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — deodorants (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea deodorants is a complete data void in this repo: no processed file, no DataPoint of any metric, and no company in the register tagged to the segment. There is no player set to rate rivalry between. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR deodorants market size, growth and shares — gaps.json rows KR/deodorants market_size + growth_yoy + cagr_forecast (suggested: euromonitor_passport, statista, korea_mfds, tavily).

passages.title: Porter buyer power — deodorants (South Korea)
passages.text: No KR deodorant channel, retail or margin evidence exists. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR deodorant channel structure and trade margins — absent.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — deodorants (South Korea)
passages.text: The listed KR ODM/OEM trio carries no segment tags and no deodorant evidence; aerosol and roll-on filling is a distinct manufacturing line from the cosmetics contract-manufacturing base the repo documents. Not rated. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR deodorant manufacturing base — absent from repo.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — deodorants (South Korea)
passages.text: With no market size and no documented regulatory pathway for deodorants in Korea, neither the prize nor the gate is measurable. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR deodorant market size and MFDS classification/pathway — absent.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — deodorants (South Korea)
passages.text: No substitution evidence exists for Korean deodorants (e.g. body mist, fragrance, or clinical treatments). Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR deodorant substitution evidence — absent (euromonitor_passport, tavily).

passages.title: Porter overall — deodorants (South Korea)
passages.text: Nothing is rateable. Korea deodorants has no DataPoint on any metric, no register entry, and no corridor relevance — the segment is unresearched, not unattractive. Note this is also a segment where Korea's export machine leaves no trace in the repo: deodorants do not appear in the MFDS segment export breakdown (skincare, colour cosmetics, body cleansing, fragrances), so even the trade-flow route to a first data point is not currently open. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Run the gaps.json KR/deodorants rows before rating any force.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — deodorants (India)
passages.text: The India deodorant segment file is empty, but the evidence is not quite absent — it is cross-booked. Vini Cosmetics, whose Fogg brand is a deodorant business, sits in the repo under fragrances (FY25 operating revenue INR 1,200cr, MEDIUM, NET_REALISATION; KKR owns 54% at a US$1.2bn valuation), and india.json sizes India fragrances as 'perfume + DEODORANT combined' (US$2.6bn, LOW). That combined basket cannot be split, so there is no deodorant-only size and no deodorant-only share for any player. Rating rivalry off a basket that bundles two categories on a LOW-confidence figure would be a definitional error, so this force stays unrated even though a leading player is identifiable. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN deodorants standalone market size and brand shares, split out of the perfume+deodorant basket — gaps.json rows IN/deodorants market_size + growth_yoy + cagr_forecast (suggested: euromonitor_passport, statista, tavily).

passages.title: Porter buyer power — deodorants (India)
passages.text: Deodorant volume in India routes through fragmented GT/MT rather than the beauty platforms the repo has measured; the Nykaa fragrance commission band (22-25%) is evidence about premium perfume listings, not about deodorant distribution. No deodorant channel DataPoint exists. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN deodorant channel split (GT/MT/q-commerce/e-commerce) and trade margins — absent.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — deodorants (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. This is the one force the repo can support, and it rests on a finding that names the category directly: mass perfume and deodorant in India are domestically filled, in contrast to premium fragrance which is import-reliant on UAE, France and Germany. A domestically filled category sitting on top of India's documented third-party contract-manufacturing base — private-label houses taking orders from ~500 units, with specialty inputs from domestic makers such as Galaxy Surfactants and Fine Organics — means a deodorant brand owner has many interchangeable fillers and low switching cost. Suppliers hold little leverage. Rated THIN because the supporting evidence is a qualitative sourcing finding, not a deodorant-specific supply or cost DataPoint. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — deodorants (India)
passages.text: Domestic fill plus a commoditised contract-manufacturing base points toward cheap entry, and the repo does record heavy capital moving into adjacent India D2C beauty (~US$757m over 18 months) — but none of that funding evidence is scoped to deodorants, and there is no deodorant market size against which to judge whether entry is attractive. The adjacent-category read is suggestive, not sufficient; it is recorded here rather than converted into a rating. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN deodorant-specific entry evidence (new brands, funding, launch record) plus market size — absent.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — deodorants (India)
passages.text: The repo's one adjacent signal is that India's fragrance sizing bundles perfume with deodorant and body mist, which is a hint that the formats compete for the same demand — the fragrances Porter read treats that as directional substitution within the combined basket. Applied to deodorants alone it would be circular, since it is the same undivided basket, so this force is left unrated here. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN deodorant vs body-mist vs mass-perfume substitution evidence at the format level — absent.

passages.title: Porter overall — deodorants (India)
passages.text: Not assessable as a standalone market. India deodorants is visible in this repo only through the fragrances basket it is bundled into and through one named player (Vini/Fogg) booked elsewhere; there is no deodorant-only size, growth, share or channel figure. The single defensible structural point is supply-side: the category is domestically filled and its manufacturing is commoditised, so an entrant would not be supplier-constrained. Everything that would determine whether entry is worthwhile — size, growth, who holds share, what the shelf costs — is missing, and the KR side is emptier still, so there is no corridor read either. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Split IN deodorants out of the perfume+deodorant basket (gaps.json IN/deodorants market_size, growth_yoy, cagr_forecast) before rating.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. No derma-specific brand shares exist, but the visible competitive cluster is dense and the pull is strong: the segment grew +13% YoY (2024, Euromonitor, HIGH) on an actives race (PDRN, exosomes, peptides), and the named players span both majors and indies — AmorePacific runs Aestura and Illiyoon, LG H&H is present, and APR (Medicube) is a listed indie, alongside Dr.Jart+ and Dr. Melaxin. Double-digit growth attracting both conglomerate derma lines and funded indies into an actives arms race reads as HIGH rivalry, though the rating rests on player visibility rather than measured shares. Evidence strength: PARTIAL. Research needed: KR dermocosmetics brand-level shares (euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter buyer power — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Derma reaches consumers through the same concentrated H&B retail (Olive Young) and online channels as skincare, plus pharmacy/clinic-adjacent routes, so channel power is present. No derma-specific channel-share or margin DataPoint exists, so the level is held at MEDIUM on structural inference. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: KR dermocosmetics channel mix and margins incl. pharmacy/clinic (euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter supplier power — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Korea's ODM base (Cosmax, Kolmar, Cosmecca) extends into actives-heavy derma formulation, keeping the make outsourced and switchable and supplier leverage low overall. The one caveat: the frontier actives driving the segment (PDRN, exosomes, peptides) can concentrate around specialised ingredient/IP suppliers, which could raise supplier power at the premium edge — but the repo has no DataPoint isolating that, so the base reading stays LOW. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: Whether frontier-actives (PDRN/exosome) supply is concentrated enough to lift supplier power (tavily, euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Cosmeceutical/derma positioning leans on efficacy claims that fall under MFDS functional-cosmetic approval — a higher regulatory bar than plain skincare — which restrains entry. Offsetting it, APR/Medicube shows a listed indie can scale a derma brand fast off the ODM base. The two forces net to MEDIUM. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: MFDS functional-cosmetic (derma-claim) approval cost/timeline (korea_mfds)

passages.title: Porter substitutes — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: The natural adjacency is aesthetic-clinic procedures and injectables (the same PDRN/exosome science originates there), but the repo holds no DataPoint measuring substitution between dermocosmetics and procedures. Left unrated per the grounding rules. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Substitution evidence between derma cosmetics and aesthetic/clinic procedures in KR (euromonitor_passport, tavily)

passages.title: Porter overall — dermocosmetics (South Korea)
passages.text: The fastest-growing KR segment on file (+13%, HIGH) with an active innovation frontier and low supplier power — genuinely dynamic — but sizing is definitionally unresolved (Korean sources ~4x apart) and the functional-cosmetic entry bar plus concentrated retail temper attractiveness. Strongest read is as a brand-incubation and corridor-export segment rather than a clean domestic-share play. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Derma/actives is India's hottest skincare fight. Domestic D2C is proven and consolidating — Minimalist reached Rs347cr revenue FY24 (+89% YoY) and was acquired by HUL at ~8.5x (~US$350mn), the benchmark derma-D2C exit — while the masstige-derma tier is the fastest-growing India cut on file (+14.6% CAGR). On top sit incumbents (Cetaphil, Skinshine) and an incoming K-derma import wave (Medicube, Aestura, Illiyoon on Nykaa/Tira). Multiple funded challengers, active M&A, and imports converging on one lane is HIGH rivalry. Evidence strength: STRONG.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Buyer power is elevated by conduit concentration specific to derma: Nykaa is effectively the exclusive gateway for the K-derma wave (Medicube omnichannel launch, Illiyoon exclusive, Aestura), and its K-beauty GMV grew +60% YoY (Q3 2025) — the platform sits astride the segment's fastest-growing supply. Add the concentrated q-commerce rail and standard commissions/MRP margins, and channel buyers hold strong leverage over derma brands. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Domestic derma D2C uses the same commoditised contract-manufacturing base as skincare (Gorgeous Cosmos / IndiaMART CMs; Galaxy Surfactants and Fine Organics for actives/surfactants), so suppliers hold little power over Indian brand owners. For imported K-derma the balance inverts — the brand depends on the Korean ODM/owner plus CDSCO clearance — so supplier power is MEDIUM specifically on the corridor-import lane. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Derma is the most-funded and most-imitated lane: the Minimalist exit set a benchmark that pulls capital in, masstige derma is growing +14.6%, and the house-of-brands model spins up derma sub-brands cheaply (Innovist's Chemist at Play) on commoditised CM. K-derma owners are also entering directly (APR launched Medicube; AmorePacific brought Illiyoon). The import lane carries CDSCO/BIS friction (MEDIUM there), but domestic and direct-K entry are both wide open. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: P&S scopes India dermacosmetics as Rx-adjacent (acne, psoriasis, scars), which points to dermatologist prescriptions and clinic treatment as the natural substitute — but no DataPoint measures that substitution flow, so the force is left unrated. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Substitution evidence: OTC dermocosmetics vs dermatologist Rx / clinic procedures in India (tavily, euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter overall — dermocosmetics (India)
passages.text: The corridor's highest-conviction whitespace — mid-price derma K-beauty into Tier 2/3 — and the most attractive of the three IN reads on demand: double-digit growth, a proven exit multiple, and confirmed corridor pull (Nykaa K-beauty GMV +60%, Medicube/Illiyoon/Aestura launching). Attractiveness is real but bounded by HIGH rivalry, HIGH buyer power (Nykaa's derma gatekeeping), and a genuinely unresolved ~7x sizing spread. Entry logic favours the corridor-import / partner-with-conduit route the whitespace itself describes. Evidence strength: STRONG.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — emerging adjacencies (South Korea)
passages.text: This segment is a container for six distinct adjacencies in taxonomy.yaml — beauty_devices, ingestible_nutricosmetics, halal_certified, ayurvedic_herbal, clean_vegan and kbeauty_derivative — and Korea has no DataPoint against any of them. No company in the register is tagged here either: APR (Medicube) appears as a KR indie brand owner and Cosmax/Kolmar/Cosmecca as ODMs, but nothing in the repo attaches any of them to devices, ingestibles or the other adjacencies. Rivalry cannot be rated across six unmeasured sub-markets. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR sizing for the adjacencies separately — beauty_devices and ingestible_nutricosmetics first, since those are where Korea is most likely to have a measurable position. gaps.json rows KR/emerging_adjacencies market_size + growth_yoy + cagr_forecast (suggested: euromonitor_passport, statista, tavily).

passages.title: Porter buyer power — emerging adjacencies (South Korea)
passages.text: No channel evidence for any Korean adjacency. Device and ingestible retail run through different gatekeepers than cosmetics (electronics/home-shopping and health-supplement channels respectively), and neither is documented here. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR channel evidence for beauty devices and nutricosmetics — absent.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — emerging adjacencies (South Korea)
passages.text: The cosmetics ODM base on file does not evidence device electronics or ingestible/supplement manufacturing, which are different supply chains under different regulators. Not rated. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR supply base for beauty devices / nutricosmetics — absent.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — emerging adjacencies (South Korea)
passages.text: Each adjacency has its own regulatory gate — devices under electrical/medical-device rules, ingestibles under food/health-functional rules — and the repo documents none of them for Korea. With no barrier evidence and no market size, entry cannot be assessed. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR regulatory pathways for beauty devices and ingestible nutricosmetics — absent.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — emerging adjacencies (South Korea)
passages.text: Substitution is the defining question for this segment — devices and ingestibles compete directly with topical skincare routines and with aesthetic procedures — and the repo carries no evidence on it for Korea. The same gap was flagged as unrateable in the KR skincare read. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR substitution evidence between topical skincare, beauty devices, ingestibles and aesthetic procedures (euromonitor_passport, tavily).

passages.title: Porter overall — emerging adjacencies (South Korea)
passages.text: Unassessable. Korea is the market where these adjacencies are most plausibly developed, which makes the void conspicuous rather than benign — but plausibility is not evidence, and no force can be rated. A further structural problem: 'emerging_adjacencies' is not one market. Any single rating over six sub-segments with different buyers, channels, supply chains and regulators would be meaningless even once data lands, so the research priority is per-sub-segment sizing, not a segment total. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Size the KR adjacencies individually (beauty_devices, ingestible_nutricosmetics, clean_vegan) rather than as one segment.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — emerging adjacencies (India)
passages.text: No India DataPoint exists for any of the six adjacencies — no size, no growth, no shares. Named players do exist in the repo for one of them (see new-entrant threat), but naming participants is not the same as measuring the intensity between them, and there is no market total to divide. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN sizing for ayurvedic_herbal and kbeauty_derivative first — these are the two adjacencies with the most India-specific relevance in taxonomy.yaml. gaps.json rows IN/emerging_adjacencies market_size + growth_yoy + cagr_forecast (suggested: euromonitor_passport, statista, tavily).

passages.title: Porter buyer power — emerging adjacencies (India)
passages.text: No channel evidence scoped to any India adjacency. The Korean-derivative brands named below sell D2C and through beauty platforms, but the repo holds no listing, commission or assortment DataPoint for them specifically, so the Nykaa and q-commerce structure documented for skincare cannot be priced onto this segment. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN channel and commission evidence for Korean-derivative D2C lines — absent.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — emerging adjacencies (India)
passages.text: There is a real, unusual split visible in the repo but not enough to rate it: one Korean-derivative Indian brand manufactures in India (Pilgrim's Korean Rice Water range is made-in-India), while another manufactures in Korea and imports (Limese's formulations are made in Korea, tuned for Indian skin). Those two models have opposite supplier-power profiles — commoditised domestic contract fill versus dependence on an overseas maker plus CDSCO clearance — and with two brands and no cost, margin or volume data, the balance between them is unknown. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Split of India Korean-derivative volume between domestic fill and Korean import, with landed-cost evidence — absent.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — emerging adjacencies (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Scoped to ONE of the six sub-segments — kbeauty_derivative. The other five (beauty_devices, ingestible_nutricosmetics, halal_certified, ayurvedic_herbal, clean_vegan) have no India evidence and are NOT covered by this rating. Within kbeauty_derivative the entry record is explicit and recent: three Indian D2C brands have already launched Korean-derivative lines — Pilgrim's Korean Rice Water range (made-in-India, vegan), Limese's Korea-manufactured formulations tuned for Indian skin, and Foxtale's Hula Hoop launched amid Korean-inspired demand as it pivots from single-label D2C to a house of brands. The capital for that is documented too: KOSE put US$30m into Foxtale, and India D2C beauty/wellness drew ~US$757m over 18 months. On the make side, brands do not need factories — private-label houses take orders from ~500 units. Named entrants, documented funding and a commoditised make is a live, low-friction entry pipeline. THIN because the evidence is a launch-and-funding record rather than a measured sub-segment: there is no kbeauty_derivative market size, so the rate of entry cannot be set against the size of the prize. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: kbeauty_derivative market size in India, and any entry evidence at all for beauty_devices, ingestible_nutricosmetics, halal_certified, ayurvedic_herbal and clean_vegan — all five are unrated here.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — emerging adjacencies (India)
passages.text: The kbeauty_derivative adjacency is itself best understood as a substitute — an India-made, India-priced alternative to imported K-beauty, which is why the brands market Korean rituals and ingredients rather than Korean origin. But the repo holds no head-to-head price, share or volume evidence between derivative lines and imported K-beauty, so the direction is describable and the pressure is not measurable. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Price and share comparison between India Korean-derivative lines and imported K-beauty SKUs — no derivative retail_price DataPoint exists.

passages.title: Porter overall — emerging adjacencies (India)
passages.text: No segment-level attractiveness call is possible, and arguably none should ever be made for this container: six adjacencies with different buyers, regulators and supply chains do not share an attractiveness read. One signal is real and worth carrying forward — the kbeauty_derivative adjacency has live, funded, named entrants and a commoditised domestic make, which is the corridor's second India-side response alongside the platform land-grab. It is also the adjacency closest to the corridor's ranked whitespace (mid-price derma K-beauty in Tier 2/3), since a made-in-India Korean-ingredient line is precisely how an entrant would hold a genuine Rs700-1500 shelf price rather than a promotion-dependent one. That is a direction, not a rating: with no size for the sub-segment, no price points for the derivative brands and no shares, the segment stays unrated. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Size kbeauty_derivative in India and capture retail_price DataPoints for Pilgrim, Limese and Hula Hoop so the derivative tier can be placed against the imported K-beauty ladder.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea fragrances has no domestic market-size, share, or company data in the repo — only tiny export figures (US$0.06bn 2025 FOB). Competitive intensity cannot be rated from export values alone. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR fragrances domestic market size and player shares (gaps.json rows: market_size, growth_yoy, cagr_forecast) must be filled before any force can be rated.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: No KR fragrance channel, retail, or trade-margin evidence exists. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR fragrance channel/retail data absent.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's general cosmetics ODM base does not extend cleanly to fine-fragrance perfumery, and no fragrance-specific supplier evidence is present. Not rated. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR fragrance supply-chain / perfumery sourcing evidence absent.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: No KR fragrance market structure or barrier evidence to assess entry against. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR fragrance market size + regulatory-barrier evidence absent.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: No KR fragrance adjacent-substitution evidence. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR fragrance substitution evidence absent.

passages.title: Porter overall — fragrances (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea fragrances is a data-void segment in this repo: export-only figures, no domestic size, shares, channel, or supplier evidence. No attractiveness read is defensible — research needed across the board. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Fill KR fragrances domestic size/growth/shares (gaps.json) before rating.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. India fragrances (~US$2.6bn perfume+deodorant, LOW) is led in mass by Vini Cosmetics/Fogg (FY25 revenue INR 1,200cr, KKR-controlled) with many domestic deo/perfume players, while a wave of D2C fragrance entrants is drawing investor money. A dominant mass player plus an active D2C challenger field indicates high intensity. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Premium/perfume distribution runs through beauty platforms taking Nykaa fragrance commission of 22-25%, while mass deodorant flows through fragmented GT/MT. Channel leverage is meaningful at the premium end but diluted across mass retail. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Premium fragrance is import-reliant — UAE is India's largest perfume-import source (HS 3303), then France/Germany for high-end oils — so premium entrants depend on overseas suppliers of oils and finished juice, raising input-side leverage. Mass perfume/deodorant is domestically filled, so the higher supplier power is scoped to the premium tier. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Mass perfume/deodorant is domestically filled via contract manufacturing and D2C fragrance is actively funded, so domestic launch is cheap and well-capitalised. Premium entrants instead face import friction (CDSCO COS-1 to COS-2 plus overseas oil sourcing), so the threat is high for domestic-fill entrants and moderated for import-led premium. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. The segment itself bundles fine perfume with deodorant/body-mist, and the dominant volume sits in cheaper deo/mist formats — evidencing substitution between premium perfume and mass deodorant within the same demand space. Substitution is directional given the combined-basket sizing. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter overall — fragrances (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. India fragrances is a growing, mass-led market with a dominant deo incumbent (Fogg) and easy domestic entry, but the premium tier an import-led K-beauty entrant would target is supplier-dependent (UAE/France) and channel-gated. Attractive on demand, but premium entry carries import and supplier friction; the KR-IN corridor flow itself is negligible. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Korea's US$1.8bn hair-care market (IMARC 2025, LOW) is anchored by AmorePacific (Mise En Scene, RYO) and LG H&H, with the ODM base enabling additional brands. Evidence is a single LOW size figure with no segment-specific shares, so intensity is inferred from the two-conglomerate structure rather than measured. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: No KR hair-care segment shares on file; brand-level share data would firm the rivalry read.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. CJ Olive Young and online are the concentrated KR retail channels, giving gatekeeper leverage, but no KR hair-care trade-margin or channel-share figure exists in the repo to size it. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: KR hair-care channel-concentration / retail-margin DataPoint absent.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Korea's three listed ODM/OEM houses (Cosmax, Kolmar, Cosmecca) and wider contract base supply hair-care formulation as readily as skincare, so brand owners face little input-side bargaining leverage. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. The ODM base lets new hair-care brands launch asset-light, the same route by which AmorePacific's hair brands and indie labels reach shelf and the corridor. No scale barrier is evident for domestic entry. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: No KR-specific adjacent-segment substitution evidence (e.g. scalp-serum crossover) is present in the repo. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR scalp-care / skinification substitution evidence not in current data (skinification findings are India-side only).

passages.title: Porter overall — hair care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Korea hair care is a modest, two-conglomerate market with low supplier power and easy entry but thin repo evidence on shares and channel. Attractive as a source of formulation and corridor SKUs rather than a well-characterised domestic entry. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. India hair care (~US$4.1bn 2026, LOW) is one of the largest BPC categories and is dominated by FMCG incumbents (HUL, Godrej) in shampoo/oils while actives-led D2C (Honasa, Innovist's Bare Anatomy) contest the premium 'skinification' edge, where specialist brands are cited as outperforming legacy FMCG. Broad incumbent scale plus D2C disruption yields high intensity. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Channel power is split: mass shampoo/oils flow through fragmented GT/MT where no single retailer dominates, while premium D2C hair care depends on beauty platforms taking Nykaa haircare commission of 20-24% and concentrated q-commerce. Gatekeeper leverage is real at the premium/D2C edge but diluted across mass distribution. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Contract manufacturing dominates D2C production, and the surfactant input critical to shampoos/cleansers comes from established domestic suppliers (Galaxy Surfactants named directly). A fragmented, capable supply base keeps input-side leverage low. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Skinification is opening an actives-led premium lane where D2C entrants outperform incumbents, contract manufacturing makes launch asset-light, and beauty D2C funding remains strong. Entry into the serum/scalp-care edge is cheap and well-capitalised. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Within the hair-growth/scalp space, ingestible supplements are documented as growing at more than twice the pace of topicals, evidencing active substitution away from traditional topical hair care toward adjacent formats. Substitution pressure is present but scoped to the hair-loss/scalp sub-space. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter overall — hair care (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. India hair care is large and growing with easy production-side entry, but incumbents own the mass base, the growth edge (skinification/serums) is already crowded with well-funded D2C, and substitution toward supplements is emerging. Attractive on size; competitive on the premium lane that suits a K-beauty entrant. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Korea's men's cosmetics market (KRW 1.16tn / ~US$0.78bn 2025, Euromonitor MEDIUM) is the world's highest per-capita men's beauty market and is served by both conglomerates' men's lines plus ODM-fed brands, but no segment-level shares exist, so intensity is inferred from the mature-market structure rather than measured. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: No KR men's-grooming brand shares on file to size rivalry precisely.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: No KR men's-grooming channel, retail-share, or trade-margin evidence is present to assess gatekeeper leverage. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR men's-grooming channel-concentration / retail-margin DataPoint absent.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Korea's three listed ODM/OEM houses supply men's grooming formulation and fill on the same competitive terms as the wider cosmetics market, keeping input-side leverage low for brand owners. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. The ODM base makes asset-light men's-grooming launches straightforward, and the market's high per-capita intensity attracts entrants. No scale barrier to domestic entry is evident. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: No KR-specific evidence on men's-dedicated products being substituted by unisex ranges or adjacent categories. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR men's-vs-unisex substitution evidence absent.

passages.title: Porter overall — mens grooming (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Korea men's grooming is a small but intense, high-per-capita market with low supplier power and easy entry, but thin repo evidence on shares and channel. Attractive as a source of proven men's-skincare formulation for the corridor rather than a well-characterised domestic entry. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. India men's grooming (INR 186.3bn / ~US$1.94bn 2025, Euromonitor HIGH, +9%) is contested by FMCG incumbents in the largest baskets (haircare, deodorants) plus razors, while men's skincare and beard care — the fastest-growing, corridor-whitespace slices — draw new D2C entrants. Established incumbency plus an emerging challenger front makes intensity high. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. E-commerce is 30-35% of urban men's-grooming sales (online ~27% share, fastest-growing), so beauty platforms and q-commerce are increasingly decisive gatekeepers, while the mass balance still moves through fragmented GT/MT. Channel leverage is rising but not yet dominant across the whole basket. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Men's-grooming D2C relies on the same fragmented third-party contract-manufacturing base (MOQs ~500 units) and domestic ingredient suppliers, so input-side bargaining power over brand owners is low. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Men's skincare is explicitly the corridor's whitespace #4 (underserved vs toiletries) and is the fastest-growing slice, so an underserved, growing lane sits open to asset-light contract-manufactured D2C and to K-beauty import entrants — with CDSCO registration the main friction for the imported route. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Men's-dedicated products compete with unisex/family grooming and the basket is shifting from toiletries toward skincare — men trading traditional shave/toiletry spend into dedicated skincare and beard care evidences substitution within the segment. Directional, given basket-definition variance. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter overall — mens grooming (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. India men's grooming is well-evidenced, growing +9%, with low supplier power and an explicit, underserved men's-skincare whitespace (corridor #4) that suits a K-beauty entrant. But incumbents own the large toiletries/deo/hair baskets, rivalry is high, and rising channel concentration adds gatekeeper cost. Attractive on the skincare whitespace specifically rather than the broad basket. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — oral care (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea oral care exists in this repo only as customs trade flow. There is no domestic retail size, no growth rate, no player shares, and only one company in the register is tagged to the segment at all (LG H&H). A single named participant and zero share data cannot support an intensity read — rating it would be industry general knowledge, not evidence. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR oral_care domestic market size, growth and brand shares — gaps.json rows KR/oral_care market_size + growth_yoy + cagr_forecast (suggested: euromonitor_passport, statista, korea_mfds, tavily).

passages.title: Porter buyer power — oral care (South Korea)
passages.text: No KR oral-care channel, retail-margin or listing-fee evidence exists. The CJ Olive Young / duty-free gatekeeper structure documented for Korean cosmetics is a health-and-beauty-retail read; oral care is a different shelf (grocery/pharmacy/mass) and the repo carries nothing that evidences where Korean dentifrice actually sells. Carrying the cosmetics channel read across would be an unevidenced transfer, so this force is left unrated. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR oral-care channel split (grocery/pharmacy/H&B/online) and trade margins — no channel DataPoint exists for this segment (euromonitor_passport, korea_mfds).

passages.title: Porter supplier power — oral care (South Korea)
passages.text: Korea's listed contract-manufacturing base — Cosmax, Kolmar Korea, Cosmecca Korea — is a colour/skincare ODM ecosystem. Nothing in the repo evidences that it extends to dentifrice or oral-hygiene production, which is a separate plant type and a separate regulatory class. Reusing the skincare supplier-power read here would be exactly the general-knowledge shortcut the grounding rules forbid. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Who manufactures Korea's HS 3306 output (US$0.079986bn FOB to world, 2024) — no oral-care supply-base DataPoint in repo (korea_mfds, tavily).

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — oral care (South Korea)
passages.text: Entry barriers cannot be assessed without either a market to enter (no domestic size) or a documented regulatory gate. Korea's MFDS pathway evidence in the repo covers cosmetics; oral care sits under a quasi-drug/dentifrice classification that is not documented here, so neither the capital nor the regulatory barrier is measurable. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR oral-care regulatory classification and entry barriers (MFDS quasi-drug pathway) — absent from repo.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — oral care (South Korea)
passages.text: No evidence of substitution into or out of Korean oral care (e.g. dental-clinic services, whitening devices) exists in the repo. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: KR oral-care substitution evidence (professional dental/whitening adjacency) — absent (euromonitor_passport, tavily).

passages.title: Porter overall — oral care (South Korea)
passages.text: No attractiveness call is defensible: four of five forces have literally no evidence base. What the trade data does establish, on a single consistent basis, is scale — Korea shipped US$0.079986bn FOB of HS 3306 oral hygiene to the world in 2024 (HIGH, UN Comtrade), against US$8.54bn FOB of skincare and US$1.51bn FOB of colour cosmetics in 2025 (HIGH, MFDS). Oral care is two orders of magnitude off the categories Korea actually exports at scale, and only US$0.000251bn of that reached India. The honest read is that this is not a segment where Korea currently competes globally at scale, and not one this repo can yet assess as a market. Evidence strength: PARTIAL. Research needed: Fill KR oral_care domestic size/growth/shares before any force is rated.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — oral care (India)
passages.text: India oral care is a large, well-known category that this repo has simply not researched: the only DataPoints are three import flows. No company in the register is tagged to oral_care on the India side — HUL's tags are skincare, hair_care, colour_cosmetics and deodorants — so the repo cannot even name the incumbent set, let alone rate the intensity between them. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN oral_care market size and brand shares, organised vs unorganised — gaps.json rows IN/oral_care market_size + growth_yoy + cagr_forecast (suggested: euromonitor_passport, statista, tavily).

passages.title: Porter buyer power — oral care (India)
passages.text: The India channel evidence this repo holds is beauty-platform-specific: Nykaa commission bands (22-26% skincare, 24-28% colour, 22-25% fragrance) and the q-commerce trio's GMV split. Oral care is a grocery/GT/MT category whose route to shelf is not documented anywhere in the repo, and the beauty-platform commission structure cannot be assumed to price it. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN oral-care channel split (GT/MT/q-commerce/pharmacy) and trade margins — no oral-care channel DataPoint exists.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — oral care (India)
passages.text: India's HS 3306 import pool was US$0.01974bn CIF in 2024 (HIGH, UN Comtrade), which is small in absolute terms — but with no market-size DataPoint for the segment, import dependence cannot be computed, and deriving one by combining these two figures is exactly what the grounding rules forbid. The contract-manufacturing structure documented for India D2C beauty is a skincare/haircare finding and carries no oral-care evidence. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN oral_care market size (to make the import pool interpretable) plus domestic manufacturing structure.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — oral care (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Scoped strictly to the import / KR-IN corridor lane — the domestic-manufacture lane, which almost certainly carries this category, is unmeasured and is NOT covered by this rating. India's entire HS 3306 import pool was US$0.01974bn CIF in 2024; Korea supplied US$0.000485bn of it and China US$0.001595bn (all HIGH, UN Comtrade), so Korea is a minor supplier even within a small import pool, and behind China. Layered on that, any imported cosmetic requires CDSCO registration (Form COS-1 to COS-2 via the SUGAM portal) plus manufacturing-site registration before a consignment clears. A near-absent Korean beachhead plus a pre-clearance gate means the corridor-import route into India oral care is not a live entrant threat, and offers no established lane for a K-origin entrant to ride. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: Domestic-lane entrant threat (contract-manufacturing availability, funding into India oral-care brands) is unrated — needs IN oral_care market structure from gaps.json.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — oral care (India)
passages.text: No substitution evidence for India oral care (e.g. traditional/unorganised alternatives such as tooth powders, or dental services) exists in the repo. This matters more than usual here because the organised/unorganised split — mandatory on every India number under the repo's rules — is itself unknown for this segment. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: IN oral-care substitution and unorganised-share evidence (tooth powder, traditional formats) — absent (euromonitor_passport, tavily).

passages.title: Porter overall — oral care (India)
passages.text: Not assessable as a market on current evidence. The only defensible structural read is corridor-shaped: the Korea-to-India oral-care flow is negligible in both directions (US$0.000251bn FOB out, US$0.000485bn CIF in, 2024 — the gap between them being the normal FOB/CIF mirror discrepancy, not two separate quantities), and China already supplies more of India's oral-care imports than Korea does. Four of five forces are unrated. Until gaps.json's IN oral_care size/growth rows are filled, this segment should be treated as unresearched rather than unattractive. Evidence strength: PARTIAL. Research needed: Fill IN oral_care market size, growth and organised-share before rating rivalry, buyer power or substitutes.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Two listed conglomerates split the organised top (LG H&H 59.9%, AmorePacific 40.1% of the summed listed-brand-owner base, 2025), but that share cut deliberately excludes an unusually deep indie long tail — COSRX, Anua (The Founders), Beauty of Joseon (Gudai Global), TirTir and APR/Medicube all compete visibly and several are recent entrants. A domestic retail market growing only +1% YoY (HIGH) against skincare-led exports up +11.6% YoY (HIGH, world #2 cosmetics exporter) means players fight over a near-flat home market while racing overseas. That combination — concentrated majors plus a crowded, fast-refreshing indie field in a stagnant domestic pool — is high rivalry. Evidence strength: STRONG.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. CJ Olive Young is the dominant health-and-beauty retail gatekeeper for domestic sell-through, and duty-free is a distinct, powerful channel (now contracting on the Chinese daigou decline) — both concentrate distribution in few hands, which raises buyer/channel power over brands. But the repo carries no numeric KR channel-share or retail-margin DataPoint, so the level is inferred from channel structure rather than measured. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: Olive Young / online / duty-free channel shares and retail trade margins for KR skincare (euromonitor_passport, korea_mfds)

passages.title: Porter supplier power — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Korea's brand-formulation supply is a deep, competitive ODM/OEM ecosystem — Cosmax, Kolmar Korea and Cosmecca Korea are all listed, scaled contract manufacturers. That commoditises production, lets a brand owner outsource the whole make with low switching cost, and is precisely what enables the indie proliferation seen in rivalry. Suppliers therefore hold little pricing leverage over brands. Rated on structural presence of the ODM base rather than on any margin/cost DataPoint. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. The same ODM depth that suppresses supplier power collapses the capital barrier to launching a skincare brand, and the recent arrival of indie names now carried across India's conduits (Anua, Beauty of Joseon, TirTir) evidences a live, low-friction entry pipeline. General (non-functional) skincare carries only light MFDS notification, not efficacy approval, so the regulatory gate is modest for basic-skincare entrants. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: No DataPoint in the repo measures cross-category substitution away from KR skincare (e.g. toward aesthetic procedures or colour cosmetics). Per the grounding rules this force is left unrated rather than guessed. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Evidence on substitution between skincare routines and aesthetic/derma procedures in KR (euromonitor_passport, tavily)

passages.title: Porter overall — skincare (South Korea)
passages.text: Structurally unattractive for a share-seeking entrant: a near-flat domestic market (+1%) with concentrated majors, a churning indie field, and near-zero barriers to entry compresses domestic economics. The real value of the KR skincare complex is as a brand-incubation and export engine (+11.6% exports, world #2), not as a domestic-share prize. Rivalry HIGH and new-entrant threat HIGH are the binding forces; low supplier power is the enabling condition, not an advantage a newcomer can capture. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — skincare (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Organised skincare is dominated at the top by non-pure-play FMCG (HUL 78.6%, Godrej 18.5%, Honasa 2.9% of the listed-brand-owner base) but is being contested underneath by a large D2C insurgency and heavy consolidation — HUL acquired Minimalist (~Rs3,000cr, 8.5x revenue) and Plum, Estee took Forest Essentials, Puig took Kama Ayurveda, KKR took Vini. A 40% mass-tier share (<Rs200: Pond's, Nivea, Himalaya, Lakme, Garnier) sits alongside a premiumising K-beauty import layer. Concentrated incumbents plus a well-funded, consolidating challenger field is high rivalry. Evidence strength: STRONG.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — skincare (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Distribution power sits with a concentrated set of platforms and gatekeepers. Nykaa charges 22-26% commission on skincare brands (plus 18% GST on top); the q-commerce access rail is concentrated in three players (Blinkit ~45-50%, Zepto ~20-25%, Instamart ~20-25%); and India MRP embeds a 25-45% trade margin per the repo's normalisation rule. Brands face powerful, few buyers between them and the shelf. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — skincare (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. India D2C skincare rarely owns factories — brands use third-party contract manufacturers / private-label houses (Gorgeous Cosmos and hundreds on IndiaMART, MOQs from ~500 units), with specialty inputs from domestic suppliers (Galaxy Surfactants, Fine Organics). Manufacturing is commoditised and switchable, and the market is ~91% domestically supplied by value, so suppliers hold little leverage over brand owners. (Imported K-beauty inverts this — see the corridor note in new-entrant threat.) Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — skincare (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Domestic entry is cheap and live: commoditised contract manufacturing plus continuing funding (~US$757m into India D2C beauty/wellness over 18 months; KOSE into Foxtale, Moxie, Antinorm) and a house-of-brands model (Innovist's Chemist at Play) keep new brands arriving despite the D2C slowdown. The offsetting friction applies only to imports — any imported cosmetic needs CDSCO registration (Form COS-1 to COS-2 via SUGAM) plus site registration and BIS IS 4707 compliance — so the import lane is MEDIUM while the domestic lane is HIGH. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — skincare (India)
passages.text: No DataPoint measures substitution pressure on India skincare specifically. Skinification of hair care (actives migrating into serums/tonics) is documented as category-blurring but is adjacency, not evidence that another category displaces facial skincare. Left unrated. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Substitution evidence for India skincare vs adjacent actives categories (euromonitor_passport, tavily)

passages.title: Porter overall — skincare (India)
passages.text: Attractive on size and growth (US$9.06bn, 2025; consolidation confirming value) but hard to enter unaided: rivalry is HIGH across both incumbents and D2C, and buyer power is HIGH because platform gatekeepers (Nykaa, q-commerce trio) and MRP trade margins tax every brand. Low supplier power favours an asset-light build, but the import lane's CDSCO friction and the platforms' leverage argue for a partner-with-conduit / corridor-import route over a cold domestic launch. Evidence strength: STRONG.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. No sun-care-specific brand shares exist in the repo, so rivalry is inferred from segment structure. Korea is a global sunscreen production and export force — MFDS sunscreen production value KRW 470.3bn (CY2025, +9.4%), Kolmar Korea's US-bound OTC sunscreen +88% (2024), Korean sun-care US e-commerce projected +43% (2025) — which signals many capable, competing manufacturers/brands rather than a settled domestic oligopoly. Absent domestic share counts, the level is held at MEDIUM: clearly contested and innovation-driven, but the underlying rivalry intensity for domestic sell-through is not measured. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: KR sun-care domestic brand shares / player count (euromonitor_passport, korea_mfds)

passages.title: Porter buyer power — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. The channel structure mirrors KR skincare — Olive Young as dominant H&B gatekeeper, online, and duty-free — so channel/buyer concentration is present, but there is no sun-care-specific channel-share or margin DataPoint. Held at MEDIUM on structural inference only. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: KR sun-care channel shares and retail margins (euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter supplier power — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Sunscreen is manufacturing- and formulation-intensive, yet Korea's ODM base specialises in exactly this — Kolmar Korea is named directly as the OTC-sunscreen contract manufacturer behind the US export surge, alongside Cosmax and Cosmecca. A deep, competitive sunscreen-capable ODM ecosystem keeps supplier leverage over brands low and switching feasible. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. Sunscreen is a 'functional cosmetic' under MFDS — it sits inside the functional-cosmetics production category (KRW 7.18tn, 40% of total) that requires efficacy/SPF approval, a real gate above plain-skincare notification. That approval bar tempers the otherwise-HIGH entry threat that Korea's ODM depth would create, netting to MEDIUM. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: MFDS functional-cosmetic sunscreen approval cost/timeline (korea_mfds)

passages.title: Porter substitutes — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: No DataPoint measures substitution of dedicated KR sunscreen by SPF-moisturisers, cushions or make-up-with-SPF. Left unrated rather than guessed. Evidence strength: INSUFFICIENT. Research needed: Evidence on SPF-moisturiser / SPF-make-up substitution for dedicated sunscreen in KR (euromonitor_passport)

passages.title: Porter overall — sun care (South Korea)
passages.text: KR sun care reads as a production/export strength rather than a domestic-share opportunity: an efficacy-regulated 'functional cosmetic' with a deep sunscreen-capable ODM base (low supplier power) that is dynamic on exports (+9.4% production, +88% Kolmar US OTC, +43% US e-commerce). Its attractiveness to an entrant is as a sourcing and corridor-export base; the domestic scale itself is uncertain (retail estimates span 2.3x, all LOW). Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter rivalry — sun care (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. The market is small and underpenetrated (US$0.58-0.89bn, 2024-25; only ~32.77% of surveyed Indians used sun care daily, 2019) but actively contested — legacy players compete with a wave of D2C sun-specialists (e.g. Innovist's Sunscoop) and a growing K-beauty import layer where Beauty of Joseon's SPF50+ is a category bestseller. Fragmentation over a still-small base reads as MEDIUM rivalry, not the HIGH seen in mainstream skincare. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter buyer power — sun care (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Sunscreen is a q-commerce hero category, which puts unusual leverage in the platforms' hands: q-commerce sunscreen is projected ~+170% in 2026 and Nykaa's platform sunscreen sales grew +85% YoY (2023). With the access rail concentrated in Blinkit/Zepto/Instamart and Nykaa, plus standard commissions and MRP trade margins, channel buyers hold strong power over sun-care brands. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter supplier power — sun care (India)
passages.text: Rating: LOW. Sunscreen brands draw on the same commoditised Indian contract-manufacturing and specialty-ingredient base as skincare (Gorgeous Cosmos / IndiaMART CMs, Galaxy Surfactants, Fine Organics). SPF formulation and BIS IS 4707 testing add some technical demand on the supplier, but do not concentrate supply enough to give manufacturers pricing power over brands. Evidence strength: THIN.

passages.title: Porter new entrant threat — sun care (India)
passages.text: Rating: HIGH. Dedicated sunscreens are baseline whitespace #2 (India sun care underpenetrated), the q-commerce surge lowers the access barrier for new brands into Tier 2/3, and cheap contract manufacturing plus live D2C funding keep domestic launches easy (Innovist's Sunscoop is a documented sun-specialist entrant). Imports face the CDSCO + BIS SPF gate (MEDIUM for that lane), but the domestic and corridor entry vectors are wide open. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.

passages.title: Porter substitutes — sun care (India)
passages.text: Rating: MEDIUM. The dominant alternative to dedicated sunscreen in India is non-consumption and casual substitution: a 2019 survey found 25.62% never use sun care and only ~32.77% use it daily, so SPF-moisturisers, BB creams and simply going without still absorb much of the occasion. That non-consumption pool is the real competitor for a dedicated-sunscreen entrant, though the supporting datapoint is a single dated survey. Evidence strength: THIN. Research needed: Current substitution split: dedicated sunscreen vs SPF-moisturiser/BB vs non-use in India (euromonitor_passport, tavily)

passages.title: Porter overall — sun care (India)
passages.text: The most corridor-favourable of the three segments on the demand side: underpenetrated, high-growth, and pulled by evidenced K-beauty sunscreen demand (Korean-sunscreen searches +148%, glass-skin +61%). Attractive for entry on growth + corridor tailwind, but tempered by a small base, HIGH buyer power (q-commerce/Nykaa gatekeeping of the hero category), and non-consumption as the standing alternative. Best pursued via the corridor-import / partner-with-conduit route that the whitespace itself implies. Evidence strength: PARTIAL.
